translations.idiomatic: Volume 222

sentences.zh: 【唐紀三十八】 起重光赤奮若，盡昭陽單閼六月，凡二年有奇。

translations.literal: [Annals of Tang, thirty-eighth] From the year Chongguang Chifenruo through the sixth month of Zhaoyang Danqie, in all a little more than two years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Annals 38] Covering a span of just over two years, from the chongguang chifenruo year through the sixth month of the zhaoyang danqie cycle.

sentences.zh: 肅宗文明武德大聖大宣孝皇帝下之下上元二年（

translations.literal: Below the second part of the reign of Emperor Suzong, the Cultured, Martial, Sage of Great Virtue and Great Proclamation, Filially Pious—second year of Shangyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Second year of Shangyuan in the latter portion of Emperor Suzong's reign (

sentences.zh: 辛丑，公元七六一年）

translations.literal: xinchou, CE 761)
translations.idiomatic: 761 CE, year xinchou)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸卯，史思明改元應天。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the day guimao, Shi Siming changed the era name to Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on guimao day in the first month, Shi Siming proclaimed the new era name Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 張景超引兵攻杭州，敗李藏用將李強於石夷門。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingchao led troops to attack Hangzhou and defeated Li Cangyong's officer Li Qiang at Shiyimen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingchao marched on Hangzhou and routed Li Qiang, a general under Li Cangyong, at Shiyimen.

sentences.zh: 孫待封自武康南出，將會景超攻杭州，溫晁據險擊敗之；

translations.literal: Sun Daifeng came south from Wukang intending to join Jingchao in attacking Hangzhou; Wen Chao held the defiles and defeated him;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Daifeng marched south from Wukang to link up with Jingchao for an assault on Hangzhou, but Wen Chao used the terrain to his advantage and beat him back;

sentences.zh: 待封脫身奔烏程，李可封以常州降。

translations.literal: Daifeng escaped and fled to Wucheng; Li Kefeng surrendered Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Daifeng broke free and fled to Wucheng, while Li Kefeng surrendered Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁未，田神功使特進楊惠元等將千五百人西擊王□恆。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Tian Shenggong sent Special Advancement Yang Huiyuan and others with fifteen hundred men west to attack Wang □heng.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day Tian Shenggong dispatched Yang Huiyuan, holder of the tejin title, and fifteen hundred troops west against Wang □heng.

sentences.zh: 辛亥夜，神功先遣特進范知新等將四千人自白沙濟，西趣下蜀；

translations.literal: On the night of xinhai, Shenggong first sent Special Advancement Fan Zhixin and others with four thousand men to cross from Baisha, heading west toward Xiashu;
translations.idiomatic: That xinhai night Shenggong sent Fan Zhixin and four thousand men across from Baisha, marching west toward Xiashu;

sentences.zh: 鄧景山等將千人自海陵濟，東趣常州；

translations.literal: Deng Jingshan and others with a thousand men crossed from Hailing, heading east toward Changzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Jingshan led a thousand men across from Hailing toward Changzhou in the east;

sentences.zh: 神功與邢延恩將三千人軍於瓜洲，壬子，濟江。

translations.literal: Shenggong and Xing Yan'en with three thousand men encamped at Guazhou; on renzi they crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Shenggong and Xing Yan'en camped at Guazhou with three thousand men and crossed the Yangtze on renzi day.

sentences.zh: 展將步騎萬餘陳於蒜山；

translations.literal: Zhan arrayed more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry at Suanshan;
translations.idiomatic: Zhan drew up over ten thousand foot and horse at Suanshan;

sentences.zh: 神功以舟載兵趣金山，會大風，五舟飄抵金山下，展屠其二舟，沉其三舟，神功不得度，還軍瓜洲。

translations.literal: Shenggong loaded troops on boats toward Jinshan; a great wind arose, five boats were driven to the foot of Jinshan—Zhan slaughtered the men on two and sank three; Shenggong could not cross and withdrew to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shenggong ferried troops toward Jinshan, but a gale drove five boats ashore at the mountain's foot; Zhan massacred two boatloads and sank the other three, forcing Shenggong to turn back to Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 而范知新等兵已至下蜀，展擊之，不勝。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Fan Zhixin's force had reached Xiashu; Zhan attacked and did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixin's column had already reached Xiashu, but Zhan repulsed their attack.

sentences.zh: 弟殷勸展引兵逃入海，可延歲月，展曰：「若事不濟，何用多殺人父子乎！

translations.literal: Younger brother Yin urged Zhan to lead the army to flee into the sea and gain months of respite; Zhan said, "If the affair will not succeed, what use is slaughtering so many fathers and sons!
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yin urged him to take the army to sea and buy time, but Zhan replied, "If we cannot succeed, why spill so much blood between fathers and sons?

sentences.zh: 死，早晚等耳！」

translations.literal: Death—early or late, it is all the same!"
translations.idiomatic: Death comes soon or late—it makes no difference!"

sentences.zh: 遂更帥眾力戰。

translations.literal: He then again led the masses in fierce battle.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied his men and fought on.

sentences.zh: 將軍賈隱林射展，中目而僕，遂斬之。

translations.literal: General Jia Yinlin shot Zhan, struck his eye, and he fell; they then beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: General Jia Yinlin shot Zhan in the eye, felling him, and Zhan was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 劉殷、許嶧等皆死。

translations.literal: Liu Yin, Xu Yi, and others all died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin, Xu Yi, and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 隱林，滑州人也。

translations.literal: Yinlin was a man of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yinlin came from Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 楊惠元等擊破王□恆於淮南，□恆引兵東走，至常熟，乃降。

translations.literal: Yang Huiyuan and others defeated Wang □heng in Huainan; □heng led troops east in flight, reached Changshu, and then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huiyuan defeated Wang □heng in Huainan; □heng fled east to Changshu and surrendered there.

sentences.zh: 孫待封詣李藏用降。

translations.literal: Sun Daifeng went to Li Cangyong and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Daifeng submitted to Li Cangyong.

sentences.zh: 張景超聚兵至七千餘人，聞展死，悉以兵授張法雷，使攻杭州，景超逃入海。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingchao had gathered more than seven thousand troops; hearing of Zhan's death, he handed all the soldiers to Zhang Falei to attack Hangzhou, while Jingchao fled into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingchao, who had mustered over seven thousand men, turned his forces over to Zhang Falei for an attack on Hangzhou after learning of Zhan's death, then escaped by sea.

sentences.zh: 法雷至杭州，李藏用擊破之，餘黨皆平。

translations.literal: Falei reached Hangzhou; Li Cangyong defeated him and the remaining partisans were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cangyong crushed Zhang Falei at Hangzhou and mopped up the rest of the rebels.

sentences.zh: 平盧軍大掠十餘日。

translations.literal: The Pinglu army plundered greatly for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: The Pinglu troops looted the region for over ten days.

sentences.zh: 安、史之亂，亂兵不及江、淮，至是，其民始罹荼毒矣。

translations.literal: In the An-Shi rebellion the rebel armies had not reached the Jiang-Huai region; only now did its people first suffer bitter affliction.
translations.idiomatic: The An Lushan–Shi Siming rebellion had spared the Jiang-Huai heartland until now, when its people at last endured devastation.

sentences.zh: 荊南節度使呂諲奏，請以江南之潭、岳、郴、邵、永、道、連，黔中之涪州，皆隸荊南；

translations.literal: Jingnan military governor Lü Yin memorialized, asking that Tan, Yue, Chen, Shao, Yong, Dao, and Lian in Jiangnan, and Fuzhou in Qianzhong, all be placed under Jingnan;
translations.idiomatic: Jingnan governor Lü Yin petitioned to annex the Jiangnan prefectures of Tan, Yue, Chen, Shao, Yong, Dao, and Lian, plus Fuzhou in Qianzhong, under his command;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 二月，奴剌、党項寇寶雞，燒大散關，南侵鳳州，殺刺史蕭心曳，大掠而西；

translations.literal: Second month, the Nula and Tangut raided Baoji, burned Dasan Pass, invaded south into Fengzhou, killed prefect Xiao Xinyi, and plundered greatly westward;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Nula and Tangut forces raided Baoji, torched Dasan Pass, pushed south into Fengzhou, killed Prefect Xiao Xinyi, and looted their way west;

sentences.zh: 鳳翔節度使李鼎追擊破之。

translations.literal: Fengxiang military governor Li Ding pursued, attacked, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang governor Li Ding chased them down and routed them.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，新羅王金嶷入朝，因請宿衛。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Silla King Kim Ni entered court and requested to remain on palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day King Kim Ni of Silla came to court and asked to stay on as an imperial guardsman.

sentences.zh: 或言：「洛中將士皆燕人，久戍思歸，上下離心，急擊之，可破也。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "The officers and soldiers in Luoyang are all men of Yan, long garrisoned and longing to return—above and below are divided in heart; strike them urgently and they can be broken."
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that Luoyang's garrison, homesick Yan men divided from their commanders, could be crushed by a swift attack.

sentences.zh: 陝州觀軍容使魚朝恩以為信然，屢言於上，上敕李光弼等進取東京。

translations.literal: Shaanzhou army-inspection commissioner Yu Chao'en believed this true and repeatedly spoke to the emperor; the emperor ordered Li Guangbi and others to advance and take the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Army-inspection commissioner Yu Chao'en of Shaanzhou bought the idea and pressed the emperor repeatedly until Li Guangbi was ordered to retake the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 光弼奏稱：「賊鋒尚銳，未可輕進。」

translations.literal: Guangbi memorialized saying, "The rebels' edge is still sharp; one must not advance lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi replied that the rebels remained formidable and warned against a rash advance.

sentences.zh: 朔方節度使僕固懷恩，勇而愎，麾下皆蕃、漢勁卒，恃功，多不法，郭子儀寬厚曲容之，每用兵臨敵，倚以集事；

translations.literal: Shuofang military governor Pugu Huai'en was brave but obstinate; under his command were all strong Tangut and Han soldiers who relied on merit and often acted lawlessly; Guo Ziyi was generous and indulged them, and whenever he used troops facing the enemy he relied on Huai'en to gather affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang governor Pugu Huai'en was brave but headstrong, leading fierce Tangut and Han veterans who flouted discipline; Guo Ziyi had indulged them and leaned on Huai'en in battle;

sentences.zh: 李光弼性嚴，一裁之以法，無所假貸。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi's nature was strict; he judged all by law with no indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi enforced the law without favor.

sentences.zh: 懷恩憚光弼而心惡之，乃附朝恩，言東都可取。

translations.literal: Huai'en feared Guangbi but hated him in heart; he therefore attached himself to Chao'en and said the Eastern Capital could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en feared Guangbi but resented him, sided with Chao'en, and insisted Luoyang was ripe for the taking.

sentences.zh: 由是中使相繼，督光弼使出師，光弼不得已，使鄭陳節度使李抱玉守河陽，與懷恩將兵會朝恩及神策節度使衛伯玉攻洛陽。

translations.literal: "Hence palace envoys came in succession, pressing Guangbi to take the field; Guangbi had no choice—he had Zheng-Chen military governor Li Baoyu hold Heyang, and with Huai'en led troops to join Chao'en and Shence military governor Wei Boyu in attacking Luoyang."
translations.idiomatic: "Imperial envoys kept pressing Guangbi to march; he left Li Baoyu to hold Heyang and joined Huai'en, Chao'en, and Shence governor Wei Boyu for the Luoyang campaign."

sentences.zh: 戊寅，陳於邙山。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, they arrayed at Mangshan.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day the allied armies formed up at Mangshan.

sentences.zh: 光弼命依險而陳，懷恩陳於平原，光弼曰：「依險則可以進，可以退；

translations.literal: Guangbi ordered deployment relying on defiles; Huai'en arrayed on the plain. Guangbi said, "Relying on defiles one can advance and can retreat;
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi wanted a defensive position on the heights while Huai'en lined up on open ground; Guangbi argued that rugged terrain allowed advance or retreat;

sentences.zh: 若平原，戰而不利則盡矣。

translations.literal: If on the plain, when battle goes unfavorably then all is lost.
translations.idiomatic: on the plain, a lost battle meant total destruction.

sentences.zh: 思明不可忽也。」

translations.literal: Siming must not be slighted."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming was not to be underestimated.

sentences.zh: 命移於險，懷恩復止之。

translations.literal: He ordered a move to defensible ground; Huai'en again stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a shift to higher ground, but Huai'en blocked it again.

sentences.zh: 史思明乘其陳未定，進兵薄之，官軍大敗，死者數千人，軍資器械盡棄之。

translations.literal: Shi Siming, while their array was not yet settled, advanced troops to press them; the government army was greatly defeated—several thousand dead, all military stores and equipment abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming struck before the formation set, routing the imperial army: thousands dead and all supplies abandoned.

sentences.zh: 光弼、懷恩渡河走保聞喜，朝恩、伯玉奔還陝，抱玉亦棄河陽走，河陽、懷州皆沒於賊。

translations.literal: Guangbi and Huai'en crossed the river and fled to secure Wenxi; Chao'en and Boyu ran back to Shan; Baoyu also abandoned Heyang and fled—Heyang and Huaizhou both fell to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi and Huai'en retreated across the river to Wenxi; Chao'en and Boyu fled to Shan; Baoyu abandoned Heyang, and both Heyang and Huaizhou fell.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞之，大懼，益兵屯陝。

translations.literal: "The court heard of it and was greatly afraid, adding troops garrisoned at Shan.
translations.idiomatic: "Terrified, the court reinforced the garrison at Shan.

sentences.zh: 李揆與呂諲同為相，不相悅。

translations.literal: Li Kui and Lü Yin served as chancellors together and were not mutually pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors Li Kui and Lü Yin were at odds.

sentences.zh: 諲在荊南，以善政聞，揆恐其復入相，奏言置軍湖南非便，又陰使人如荊、湖求諲過失。

translations.literal: Yin in Jingnan was known for good governance; Kui feared he would again enter the chancellorship, memorialized that establishing armies in Hunan was inconvenient, and also secretly sent men to Jing and Hu to seek Yin's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's reputation in Jingnan made Kui fear his return to court; Kui attacked his Hunan garrison plan and sent agents to dig up dirt.

sentences.zh: 諲上疏訟揆罪，癸未，貶揆袁州長史，以河中節度使蕭華為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Yin submitted a memorial accusing Kui; on guiwei, Kui was demoted to Yuanzhou chief administrator; Hedong military governor Xiao Hua was made Zhongshu vice director and fellow Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Yin impeached Kui in a memorial; on guiwei day Kui was exiled to Yuanzhou and Hedong governor Xiao Hua joined the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 史思明猜忍好殺，群下小不如意，動至族誅，人不自保。

translations.literal: Shi Siming was suspicious, cruel, and fond of killing; if subordinates were slightly displeasing, he often exterminated whole clans—men could not protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming was paranoid and bloodthirsty, routinely wiping out entire families over minor slights until no one felt safe.

sentences.zh: 朝義，其長子也，常從思明將兵，頗謙謹，愛士卒，將士多附之；

translations.literal: Chaoyi was his eldest son, often following Siming in leading troops, quite modest and cautious, loving the soldiers—the officers and men mostly attached to him;
translations.idiomatic: His eldest Chaoyi campaigned with him, modest and caring toward the ranks, and won broad loyalty;

sentences.zh: 無寵于思明，思明愛少子朝清，使守范陽，常欲殺朝義，立朝清為太子，左右頗洩其謀。

translations.literal: He had no favor from Siming; Siming loved the younger son Chaoqing, had him guard Fanyang, often wished to kill Chaoyi and install Chaoqing as heir apparent—the attendants largely leaked this plot.
translations.idiomatic: Siming favored younger son Chaoqing at Fanyang and plotted to kill Chaoyi and name Chaoqing heir—a plan his courtiers leaked.

sentences.zh: 思明既破李光弼，欲乘勝西入關，使朝義將兵為前鋒，自北道襲陝城，思明自南道將大軍繼之。

translations.literal: Siming having defeated Li Guangbi, wished to ride victory west into the passes—he had Chaoyi lead troops as vanguard, himself striking Shaan city by the northern route while Siming from the southern route led the great army after.
translations.idiomatic: After beating Guangbi, Siming planned a two-pronged drive into the passes: Chaoyi as vanguard against Shaan city from the north, Siming following with the main force from the south.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲午，朝義兵至礓子嶺，衛伯玉逆擊，破之。

translations.literal: Third month, on the day jiawu, Chaoyi's troops reached Jiangziling; Wei Boyu met and attacked, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiawu day, Chaoyi reached Jiangziling and Wei Boyu repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 朝義數進兵，皆為陝兵所敗。

translations.literal: Chaoyi several times advanced troops—all were defeated by the Shan troops.
translations.idiomatic: Every thrust Chaoyi made was beaten back by the Shaan garrison.

sentences.zh: 思明退屯永寧，以朝義為怯，曰：「終不足成吾事！」

translations.literal: Siming withdrew and encamped at Yongning, deeming Chaoyi cowardly, saying, "In the end he is insufficient to accomplish my affair!"
translations.idiomatic: Siming pulled back to Yongning, called Chaoyi cowardly, and snapped, "He will never finish what I started!

sentences.zh: 欲按軍法斬朝義及諸將。

translations.literal: He wished to apply military law and behead Chaoyi and the various generals.
translations.idiomatic: He threatened to execute Chaoyi and his generals under military law.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，命朝義築三隅城，欲貯軍糧，期一日畢，朝義築畢，未泥，思明至，詬怒之，令左右立馬監泥，斯須而畢。

translations.literal: On wuxu he ordered Chaoyi to build a three-corner fort to store army grain, fixed one day for completion; Chaoyi finished building but had not plastered; Siming arrived, reviled and raged, ordered attendants on horseback to supervise plastering—in a moment it was done.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu he ordered Chaoyi to build a triangular granary fort in one day; when Chaoyi finished the walls but not the plaster, Siming cursed him and had cavalry oversee the work until it was done in minutes.

sentences.zh: 思明又曰：「俟克陝州，終斬此賊。」

translations.literal: Siming also said, "When Shaanzhou is taken, in the end I will behead this villain."
translations.idiomatic: Siming added, "Once Shaanzhou falls, I will kill this wretch.

sentences.zh: 朝義憂懼，不知所為。

translations.literal: Chaoyi was worried and afraid, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi was terrified and at a loss.

sentences.zh: 思明在鹿橋驛，令腹心曹將軍將兵宿衛；

translations.literal: Siming was at Luqiao Post; he ordered his trusted General Cao to lead troops on night guard;
translations.idiomatic: Siming lodged at Luqiao Post with his trusted General Cao commanding the guard;

sentences.zh: 朝義宿於逆旅，其部將駱悅、蔡文景說朝義曰：「悅等與王，死無日矣！

translations.literal: Chaoyi lodged at an inn; his subordinate generals Luo Yue and Cai Wenjing said to Chaoyi, "Yue and company with Your Highness—death is not days away!
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi stayed at an inn while generals Luo Yue and Cai Wenjing warned him, "We and you, my prince, are living on borrowed time!

sentences.zh: 自古有廢立，請召曹將軍謀之。」

translations.literal: Since antiquity there has been deposition and installation—please summon General Cao to plan it."
translations.idiomatic: Deposing rulers is an old story—summon General Cao and plot with us.

sentences.zh: 朝義俯首不應。

translations.literal: Chaoyi bowed his head and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi looked down and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 悅等曰：「王苟不許，悅等今歸李氏，王亦不全矣。」

translations.literal: Yue and company said, "If Your Highness will not consent, Yue and company will now return to the Li house—and Your Highness also will not remain whole."
translations.idiomatic: They pressed him: refuse, and we defect to the Tang—and you will not survive either.

sentences.zh: 朝義泣曰：「諸君善為之，勿驚聖人！」

translations.literal: Chaoyi wept and said, "Gentlemen, handle it well—do not alarm the Sage!"
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, Chaoyi said, "Do as you must, but do not frighten my father!"

sentences.zh: 悅等乃令許叔冀之子季常召曹將軍，至，則以其謀告之；

translations.literal: Yue and company then had Xu Shuji's son Jichang summon General Cao; when he arrived they told him the plot;
translations.idiomatic: They sent Xu Shuji's son Jichang to fetch General Cao and confided the plan.

sentences.zh: 曹將軍知諸將盡怨，恐禍及己，不敢違。

translations.literal: General Cao knew the generals were all resentful, feared disaster reaching himself, and did not dare refuse.
translations.idiomatic: General Cao, knowing the officers' rage and fearing for himself, went along.

sentences.zh: 是夕，悅等以朝義部兵三百被甲詣驛，宿衛兵怪之，畏曹將軍，不敢動。

translations.literal: That evening Yue and company with three hundred of Chaoyi's armored troops went to the post; the guard troops found it strange but feared General Cao and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: That night three hundred of Chaoyi's armored men marched on the post; the guards were uneasy but dared not move against General Cao.

sentences.zh: 悅等引兵入至思明寢所，值思明如廁，問左右，未及對，已殺數人，左右指示之。

translations.literal: Yue and company led troops in to Siming's sleeping quarters; they happened upon Siming going to the privy; they asked attendants, and before they answered had already killed several—attendants pointed him out.
translations.idiomatic: They burst into Siming's quarters as he was heading to the privy, killed attendants who hesitated, and were directed to him.

sentences.zh: 思明聞有變，逾垣至廄中，自備馬乘之，悅人兼人周子俊射之，中臂，墜馬，遂擒之。

translations.literal: Siming heard there was trouble, climbed over the wall to the stable, saddled a horse himself and mounted; Yue's man Jianren Zhou Zijun shot him, hit the arm, he fell from the horse, and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Siming vaulted into the stable and mounted a horse, but Zhou Zijun shot him in the arm, pulled him down, and seized him.

sentences.zh: 思明問：「亂者為誰？」

translations.literal: Siming asked, "Who are the rebels?"
translations.idiomatic: Siming asked who was revolting.

sentences.zh: 悅曰：「奉懷王命。」

translations.literal: Yue said, "Obeying the Prince of Huai's command."
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yue answered, "We act for the Prince of Huai.

sentences.zh: 思明曰：「我朝來語失，宜其及此。

translations.literal: Siming said, "My words this morning were wrong—it is fitting I come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Siming said, "My harsh words this morning brought this on me.

sentences.zh: 然殺我太早，何不待我克長安！

translations.literal: Yet to kill me too early—why not wait until I took Chang'an!
translations.idiomatic: But you kill me too soon—why not wait until I had taken Chang'an?

sentences.zh: 今事不成矣。」

translations.literal: Now the affair cannot succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Now nothing will succeed.

sentences.zh: 悅等送思明於柳泉驛，囚之，還報朝義曰：「事成矣」。

translations.literal: Yue and company sent Siming to Liuquan Post and imprisoned him, returned and reported to Chaoyi, "The affair is accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: They held Siming at Liuquan Post and told Chaoyi, "It is done."

sentences.zh: 朝義曰：「不驚聖人乎？」

translations.literal: Chaoyi said, "Did you not alarm the Sage?"
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi asked, "Was my father frightened?

sentences.zh: 悅曰：「無。」

translations.literal: Yue said, "No."
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yue said no.

sentences.zh: 時周摯、許叔冀將後軍在福昌，悅等使許季常往告之，摯驚倒於地；

translations.literal: At that time Zhou Zhi and Xu Shuji were leading the rear army at Fuchang; Yue and company sent Xu Jichang to tell them—Zhi was startled and fell to the ground;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhi and Xu Shuji commanded the rear at Fuchang; when told the news Zhou Zhi collapsed.

sentences.zh: 朝義引軍還，摯、叔冀來迎，悅等勸朝義執摯，殺之。

translations.literal: Chaoyi led the army back; Zhi and Shuji came to welcome; Yue and company urged Chaoyi to seize Zhi and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: As Chaoyi marched back, Yue urged him to seize and kill Zhou Zhi when he came to greet them.

sentences.zh: 軍至柳泉，悅等恐眾心未壹，遂縊殺思明，以氈裹其屍，橐駝負歸洛陽。

translations.literal: When the army reached Liuquan, Yue and company feared hearts were not united and therefore strangled Siming, wrapped his corpse in felt, and had camels carry it back to Luoyang."
translations.idiomatic: At Liuquan, fearing unrest, they strangled Siming, wrapped his body in felt, and loaded it on camels for Luoyang."

sentences.zh: 朝義即皇帝位，改元顯聖。

translations.literal: Chaoyi immediately took the emperor's position and changed the era name to Xiansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi proclaimed himself emperor and adopted the era name Xiansheng.

sentences.zh: 密使人至范陽，敕散騎常侍張通儒等殺朝清及朝清母辛氏並不附己者數十人。

translations.literal: He secretly sent men to Fanyang, ordering Palace Attendant Zhang Tongru and others to kill Chaoqing and Chaoqing's mother Lady Xin and several tens who did not attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: Secret orders went to Fanyang for Zhang Tongru to kill Chaoqing, his mother Lady Xin, and dozens of dissenters.

sentences.zh: 其黨自相攻擊，戰城中數月，死者數千人，范陽乃定。

translations.literal: His factions mutually attacked; they fought in the city for months—several thousand dead—and Fanyang was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Factions fought in the streets for months, thousands died, and Fanyang finally quieted.

sentences.zh: 朝義以其將柳城李懷仙為范陽尹、燕京留守。

translations.literal: Chaoyi made his general Li Huaixian of Liucheng Fanyang prefect and Yanjing regent.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi appointed Li Huaixian of Liucheng as Fanyang prefect and regent of Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 時洛陽四面數百里，州、縣皆為丘墟，而朝義所部節度使皆安祿山舊將，與思明等夷，朝義召之，多不至，略相羈縻而已，不能得其用。

translations.literal: At that time for several hundred li around Luoyang, prefectures and counties were all ruins; yet the military governors under Chaoyi were all old An Lushan generals, equals to Siming and the like—Chaoyi summoned them but many did not come; he only loosely kept them on reins and could not obtain their use.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's hinterland lay in ruins, and Chaoyi's governors—veterans of An Lushan no less proud than Siming—mostly ignored his summons, leaving him little real authority.

sentences.zh: 李光弼上表，固求自貶；

translations.literal: Li Guangbi submitted a memorial firmly requesting self-demotion;
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi repeatedly asked to be demoted after the defeat.

sentences.zh: 制以開府儀同三司、侍中，領河中節度使。

translations.literal: An edict made him Kaifu Yitong Sansi, Palace Attendant, and concurrent Hedong military governor.
translations.idiomatic: The throne named him Kaifu Yitong Sansi and Palace Attendant while keeping him as Hedong governor.

sentences.zh: 術士長塞鎮將朱融與左武衛將軍竇如玢等謀奉嗣岐王珍作亂，金吾將軍邢濟告之。

translations.literal: Daoist priest and Changsai garrison officer Zhu Rong with Left Martial Guard general Dou Rubin and others plotted to install the heir Prince of Qi Zhen in rebellion; Jinwu general Xing Ji reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerer and garrison officer Zhu Rong joined Left Martial Guard general Dou Rubin in a plot to put heir Prince Zhen of Qi on the throne; Jinwu general Xing Ji exposed them.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙卯朔，廢珍為庶人，溱州安置，其黨皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, first day of the month yimao, Zhen was deposed as commoner and settled at Qinzhou; his faction all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the first yimao day of the fourth month, Zhen was reduced to commoner status and exiled to Qinzhou; his co-conspirators were executed.

sentences.zh: 珍，業之子也。

translations.literal: Zhen was Ye's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was the son of Ye.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，左散騎常侍張鎬貶辰州司戶。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Left Palace Attendant Zhang Hao was demoted to Chenzhou registrar.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day Zhang Hao, left palace attendant, was banished to registrar of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 鎬嘗買珍宅故也。

translations.literal: Hao had once bought Zhen's residence—hence this.
translations.idiomatic: He had bought Zhen's house, which tied him to the plot.

sentences.zh: 己未，以吏部侍郎裴遵慶為黃門侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, Libu vice director Pei Zunqing was made Huangmen vice director and fellow Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day Pei Zunqing rose from vice minister of personnel to vice director of the Chancellery and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，青密節度使尚衡破史朝義兵，斬首五千餘級。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, Qing-Mi military governor Shang Heng defeated Shi Chaoyi's troops and cut off more than five thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day Shang Heng, governor of Qing and Mi, routed Chaoyi's army and took five thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，兗鄆節度使能元皓破朝義兵。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, Yan-Yun military governor Neng Yuanhao defeated Chaoyi's troops.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day Neng Yuanhao of Yan-Yun defeated Chaoyi's forces.

sentences.zh: 壬午，梓州刺史段子璋反，子璋驍勇，從上皇在蜀有功，東川節度使李奐奏替之，子璋舉兵，襲奐於綿州。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, Zizhou prefect Duan Zizhang rebelled—Zizhang was fierce and brave, had followed the retired emperor in Shu with merit; Dongchuan military governor Li Huan memorialized to replace him; Zizhang raised troops and struck Huan at Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day Zizhou prefect Duan Zizhang revolted; a veteran of the emperor's flight to Shu, he took up arms when Dongchuan governor Li Huan tried to remove him, attacking Huan at Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 道過遂州，剌史虢王巨蒼黃修屬郡禮迎之，子璋殺之。

translations.literal: Passing through Suizhou, prefect Prince of Guo Ju in flustered haste repaired the subordinate commandery's rites to welcome him; Zizhang killed him.
translations.idiomatic: En route through Suizhou, Prefect Prince Ju of Guo hurried to receive him with full ceremony; Zizhang had him killed.

sentences.zh: 李奐戰敗，奔成都，子璋自稱梁王，改元黃龍，以綿州為龍安府，置百官，又陷劍州。

translations.literal: Li Huan was defeated in battle and fled to Chengdu; Zizhang styled himself King of Liang, changed the era name to Huanglong, made Mianzhou Long'an Prefecture, established the hundred offices, and also captured Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huan fled to Chengdu after defeat; Zizhang proclaimed himself King of Liang, took the era name Huanglong, made Mianzhou his capital as Long'an, set up a full court, and seized Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，己丑，李光弼自河中入朝。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on the day jichou, Li Guangbi from Hedong entered court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jichou day, Li Guangbi came to court from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 初，李輔國與張後同謀遷上皇於西內。

translations.literal: Initially, Li Fuguo and Empress Zhang together plotted to move the retired emperor to the Western Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuguo and Empress Zhang had conspired to confine the retired emperor in the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 是日端午，山人李唐見上，上方抱幼女，謂唐曰：「朕念之，卿勿怪也。」

translations.literal: That day was the Dragon Boat Festival; mountain man Li Tang saw the emperor—the emperor was just holding a young daughter and said to Tang, "I miss her; do not take it amiss, sir."
translations.idiomatic: On Dragon Boat Festival day the recluse Li Tang was received; the emperor held a little princess and said, "I dote on her—do not be offended."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「太上皇思見陛下，計亦如陛下之念公主也。」

translations.literal: He replied, "The Retired Emperor longs to see Your Majesty—I reckon it is just as Your Majesty misses the princess."
translations.idiomatic: Tang answered, "The retired emperor longs to see you as much as you miss your daughter."

sentences.zh: 上泫然泣下，然畏張後，尚不敢詣西內。

translations.literal: The emperor wept with tears falling, yet feared Empress Zhang and still did not dare go to the Western Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept but, fearing Empress Zhang, still dared not visit the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，党項寇寶雞。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, Tangut raided Baoji.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day Tangut forces raided Baoji.

sentences.zh: 初，史思明以其博州刺史令狐彰為滑鄭汴節度使，將數千兵戍滑台。

translations.literal: Initially, Shi Siming made his Bozhou prefect Linghu Zhang military governor of Hua, Zheng, and Bian, leading several thousand troops to garrison Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Siming had appointed his Bozhou prefect Linghu Zhang to guard Huatai as governor of Hua, Zheng, and Bian with several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 彰密因中使楊萬定通表請降，徙屯杏園度。

translations.literal: Zhang secretly through palace envoy Yang Wanding sent a memorial requesting surrender and moved to encamp at Xingyuan Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang secretly petitioned to surrender through envoy Yang Wanding and shifted camp to Xingyuan Ford.

sentences.zh: 思明疑之，遣其將薛岌圍之。

translations.literal: Siming suspected him and sent his general Xue Ji to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Siming sent Xue Ji to besiege him.

sentences.zh: 彰與岌戰，大破之，因隨萬定入朝。

translations.literal: Zhang fought Ji and greatly defeated him, then followed Wanding into court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang routed Xue Ji and entered court with Wanding.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以彰為滑、衛等六州節度使。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Zhang was made military governor of six prefectures including Hua and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day Linghu Zhang was named governor of six prefectures including Hua and Wei.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，平盧節度使侯希逸擊史朝義范陽兵，破之。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Pinglu military governor Hou Xiyi attacked Shi Chaoyi's Fanyang troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day Hou Xiyi of Pinglu defeated Chaoyi's Fanyang army.

sentences.zh: 乙未，西川節度使崔光遠與東川節度使李奐共攻綿州，庚子，拔之，斬段子璋。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Xichuan military governor Cui Guangyuan and Dongchuan military governor Li Huan jointly attacked Mianzhou; on gengzi they took it and beheaded Duan Zizhang.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guangyuan and Li Huan besieged Mianzhou; on gengzi day they took the city and executed Duan Zizhang.

sentences.zh: 復以李光弼為河南副元帥、太尉兼侍中，都統河南、淮南東西、山南東、荊南、江南西、浙江東西八道行營節度，出鎮臨淮。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi was again made Henan deputy supreme commander, Grand Marshal concurrent Palace Attendant, overall commander of eight circuit campaign armies—Henan, east and west Huainan, eastern Shannan, Jingnan, western Jiangnan, east and west Zhejiang—and went out to garrison Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi was restored as deputy supreme commander of Henan, grand marshal and palace attendant, placed over eight regional commands, and posted to Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲寅，青密節度使能元皓敗史朝義將李元遇。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on the day jiayin, Qing-Mi military governor Neng Yuanhao defeated Shi Chaoyi's general Li Yuanyu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiayin day, Neng Yuanhao defeated Chaoyi's general Li Yuanyu.

sentences.zh: 江淮都統李峘畏失守之罪，歸咎於浙西節度使侯令儀，丙子，令儀坐除名，長流康州；

translations.literal: Jiang-Huai overall commander Li Xian feared guilt for losing posts and blamed Zhexi military governor Hou Lingyi; on bingzi, Lingyi was punished by removal from the rolls and long exile to Kangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian, fearing blame for lost territory, scapegoated Zhexi governor Hou Lingyi, who on bingzi day was stripped of rank and exiled to Kangzhou;

sentences.zh: 加田神功開府儀同三司，徙徐州刺史；

translations.literal: Tian Shenggong was promoted to Kaifu Yitong Sansi and transferred to Xuzhou prefect;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Shenggong was made Kaifu Yitong Sansi and moved to Xuzhou;

sentences.zh: 征李峘、鄧景山還京師。

translations.literal: Li Xian and Deng Jingshan were summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian and Deng Jingshan were recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，党項寇好畤。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Tangut raided Hao zhi.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day Tangut raiders struck Hao zhi.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸未朔，日有食之，既，大星皆見。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, first day of the month guiwei—there was an eclipse of the sun; when it ended, all the great stars were visible.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the first guiwei day of the seventh month, a total solar eclipse ended to reveal the major stars.

sentences.zh: 以試少府監李藏用為浙西節度副使。

translations.literal: Trial Director of the Palace Storehouse Li Cangyong was made Zhexi military governor deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cangyong was appointed deputy governor of Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 八月，癸丑朔，加開府儀同三司李輔國兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Eighth month, first day guichou—Kaifu Yitong Sansi Li Fuguo was added Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: On the first guichou day of the eighth month Li Fuguo was also named minister of war.

sentences.zh: 乙未，輔國赴上，宰相朝臣皆送之，御廚具饌，太常設樂。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Fuguo went to audience; chancellors and court officials all saw him off—the imperial kitchen provided food, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set up music.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuguo went to court on yiwei day, the whole bureaucracy escorted him with imperial feast and ceremonial music.

sentences.zh: 輔國驕縱日甚，求為宰相。

translations.literal: Fuguo's arrogance and license grew daily; he sought to be chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo grew ever more arrogant and demanded a seat on the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「以卿之功，何官不可為，其如朝望未允何！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Given your merit, what office could you not hold—but what of court opinion not yet assenting!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Your service entitles you to any post—but the court is not ready to accept this."

sentences.zh: 輔國乃諷僕射裴冕等薦己。

translations.literal: Fuguo then hinted Vice Director Pei Mian and others to recommend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo pressed Vice Director Pei Mian and others to nominate him.

sentences.zh: 上密謂蕭華曰：「輔國求為宰相，若公卿表來，不得不與。」

translations.literal: The emperor secretly told Xiao Hua, "Fuguo seeks the chancellorship—if the high officials submit a memorial, I must grant it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor confided to Xiao Hua that if the officials petitioned for Fuguo, he would have to agree.

sentences.zh: 華出，問冕，曰：「初無此事，吾臂可斷，宰相不可得！」

translations.literal: Hua went out and asked Mian, who said, "There was never such a thing—my arm may be cut off, but chancellor cannot be obtained!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Hua asked Pei Mian, who declared he would lose an arm before making Fuguo chancellor.

sentences.zh: 華入言之，上大悅；

translations.literal: Hua entered and reported; the emperor was greatly pleased;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Hua reported this and the emperor was delighted;

sentences.zh: 輔國銜之。

translations.literal: "Fuguo harbored resentment."
translations.idiomatic: "Fuguo never forgave him."

sentences.zh: 己巳，李光弼赴河南行營。

translations.literal: On jisi, Li Guangbi went to the Henan campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day Guangbi took command at the Henan field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以殿中監李若幽為朔方、鎮西、北庭、興平、陳鄭等節度行營及河中節度使，鎮絳州，賜名國貞。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Palace Supervisor Li Ruoyou was made Shuofang, Zhenxi, Beiting, Xingping, Chen-Zheng and other circuit campaign armies commander and Hedong military governor, garrisoning Jiangzhou, granted the name Guozhen.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day Li Ruoyou was named Guozhen, given Shuofang and allied commands, and posted to Jiangzhou as Hedong governor.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲申，天成地平節。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on the day jiashen, the festival of Heaven's Completion and Earth's Pacification.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Tian Cheng Di Ping festival was observed on jiashen day.

sentences.zh: 上於三殿置道場，以宮人為佛菩薩，北門武士為金剛神王，召大臣膜拜圍繞。

translations.literal: The emperor set up a ritual arena in the Three Halls, used palace women as Buddha and bodhisattvas, Northern Gate warriors as vajra spirit kings, and summoned great ministers to prostrate in worship surrounding them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Three Halls the emperor staged a Buddhist rite with palace women as bodhisattvas, gate guards as vajra kings, and ministers prostrating around them.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，制去尊號，但稱皇帝；

translations.literal: On renyin, an edict removed honorific titles, calling oneself only Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day an edict stripped honorific titles, leaving only "Emperor";

sentences.zh: 去年號，但稱元年；

translations.literal: removed era names, calling only First Year;
translations.idiomatic: era names were dropped in favor of "First Year";

sentences.zh: 以建子月為歲首，月皆以所建為數；

translations.literal: took the jianzi month as year start, months all numbered by their jian designation;
translations.idiomatic: the calendar year began in the jianzi month with months renumbered accordingly;

sentences.zh: 因赦天下。

translations.literal: and thereby amnestied the realm.
translations.idiomatic: and a general amnesty followed.

sentences.zh: 停京兆、河南、太原、鳳翔四京及江陵南都之號。

translations.literal: The designations of the four capitals—Jingzhao, Henan, Taiyuan, Fengxiang—and Jiangling Southern Capital were suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The titles of the four capitals and the southern capital at Jiangling were abolished.

sentences.zh: 自今每除五品以上清望京官及郎官、御史、刺史，令舉一人自代，觀其所舉，以行殿最。

translations.literal: From now, whenever appointing capital officials of fifth rank and above, court gentlemen, editors, censors, or prefects, require one person to be nominated to replace oneself—observe whom they nominate to conduct merit review.
translations.idiomatic: All future appointments from fifth rank up would require each official to name a successor candidate for performance review.

sentences.zh: 江、淮大饑，人相食。

translations.literal: The Jiang-Huai region suffered great famine; people ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Famine ravaged the Jiang-Huai region until people resorted to cannibalism.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，江淮都統崔圓署李藏用為楚州刺史。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, Jiang-Huai overall commander Cui Yuan commissioned Li Cangyong as Chuzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Cui Yuan, overall commander of Jiang-Huai, named Li Cangyong prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會支度租庸使以劉展之亂，諸州用倉庫物無准，奏請征驗。

translations.literal: It happened that the revenue and corvée commissioner, because of Liu Zhan's rebellion, found the various prefectures' use of storehouse goods without standard—memorialized requesting verification and collection.
translations.idiomatic: The revenue commissioner, citing Liu Zhan's revolt, ordered audits of prefectural storehouses.

sentences.zh: 時倉猝募兵，物多散亡，征之不足，諸將往往賣產以償之。

translations.literal: At the time they had hastily recruited troops from stores; goods were mostly scattered and lost—collection was insufficient, and generals often sold property to make repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Hasty wartime levies had depleted stores; generals sold land to cover shortages.

sentences.zh: 藏用恐其及己，嘗與人言，頗有悔恨。

translations.literal: Cangyong feared it would reach himself; he once spoke with others and showed much regret.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he would be targeted, Cangyong voiced bitter regret.

sentences.zh: 其牙將高干挾故怨，使人詣廣陵告藏用反，先以兵襲之，藏用走，干追斬之。

translations.literal: His yamen officer Gao Gan, holding an old grudge, sent men to Yangzhou to report Cangyong's rebellion, first attacking him with troops; Cangyong fled and Gan pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yamen officer Gao Gan, nursing a grudge, denounced Cangyong as a rebel at Yangzhou, attacked him, and cut him down as he fled.

sentences.zh: 崔圓遂簿責藏用將吏以驗之，將吏畏，皆附成其狀。

translations.literal: Cui Yuan then registered and pressed Cangyong's officers to verify—the officers feared and all went along to confirm the charge.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan interrogated Cangyong's staff, who confirmed the accusation out of fear.

sentences.zh: 獨孫待封堅言不反，圓命引出斬之。

translations.literal: Only Sun Daifeng firmly said he had not rebelled; Yuan ordered him led out and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Only Sun Daifeng denied guilt and was executed on Yuan's order.

sentences.zh: 或謂曰：「子何不從眾以求生！」

translations.literal: Someone said to him, "Why do you not follow the crowd to seek life!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged him to go along with the others to save his life.

sentences.zh: 待封曰：「吾始從劉大夫，奉詔書來赴鎮，人謂吾反；

translations.literal: Daifeng said, "I first followed Grandee Liu, came by imperial edict to take up the post—people said I rebelled;
translations.idiomatic: Daifeng replied, "When I followed Minister Liu here by imperial order, I was called a rebel;

sentences.zh: 李公起兵滅齊大夫，今又以李公為反。

translations.literal: Li Gong raised troops and destroyed Grandee Qi—now again Li Gong is called rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Cangyong destroyed Liu, Li too was called a rebel.

sentences.zh: 如此，誰則非反者，庸有極乎！

translations.literal: Like this, who then is not a rebel—is there any limit!
translations.idiomatic: If this goes on, who is not a rebel—and where does it end?

sentences.zh: 吾寧就死，不能誣人以非罪。」

translations.literal: I would rather accept death than falsely accuse people of crimes they did not commit."
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die than falsely condemn others.

sentences.zh: 遂斬之。

translations.literal: He was then beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: He was beheaded."

sentences.zh: 建子月，壬午朔，上受朝賀，如正旦儀。

translations.literal: Jianzi month, first day renwu—the emperor received court congratulations, as on New Year's rites.
translations.idiomatic: On the first renwu day of the jianzi month the emperor held a New Year's-style audience.

sentences.zh: 或告鴻臚卿康謙與史朝義通，事連司農卿嚴莊，俱下獄。

translations.literal: Someone reported Honglu Director Kang Qian communicating with Shi Chaoyi—the matter implicated Sinong Director Yan Zhuang; both were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Qian of Honglu was accused of dealing with Chaoyi, implicating Yan Zhuang of Sinong; both were jailed.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹劉晏遣吏防守莊家。

translations.literal: Jingzhao prefect Liu Yan sent officials to guard Zhuang's house.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao prefect Liu Yan posted guards at Zhuang's home.

sentences.zh: 上尋敕出莊，引見。

translations.literal: The emperor soon ordered Zhuang released and received him in audience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon released Zhuang and received him.

sentences.zh: 莊怨晏，因言晏與臣言，常道禁中語，矜功怨上。

translations.literal: Zhuang resented Yan and therefore said Yan in speaking with ministers often repeated palace secrets, boasted of merit, and resented the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang, resentful, accused Yan of repeating palace secrets, boasting, and disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，貶晏通州刺史，莊難江尉，謙伏誅。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Yan was demoted to Tongzhou prefect, Zhuang to Nanjiang district magistrate, Qian was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day Yan was exiled to Tongzhou, Zhuang to Nanjiang, and Qian was executed.

sentences.zh: 戊子，御史中丞元載為戶部侍郎，充句當度支、鑄錢、鹽鐵兼江淮轉運等使。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Censor-in-Chief Yuan Zai was made Hubu vice director, charged with managing revenue, coinage, salt and iron, and concurrent Jiang-Huai transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day Yuan Zai became vice minister of revenue and took over transport and fiscal affairs on the Jiang-Huai.

sentences.zh: 載初為度支郎中，敏悟善奏對，上愛其才，委以江淮漕運，數月，遂代劉晏，專掌財利。

translations.literal: Zai had initially been a revenue section director—keen and good at memorial responses; the emperor loved his talent and entrusted him with Jiang-Huai canal transport; within months he replaced Liu Yan and solely managed finances.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai, a sharp revenue official, won the emperor's favor, took over Jiang-Huai grain transport within months, and displaced Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，冬至；

translations.literal: On wuxu, the winter solstice;
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day came the winter solstice;

sentences.zh: 己亥，上朝上皇於西內。

translations.literal: on jihai the emperor attended the retired emperor at the Western Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: on jihai the emperor visited the retired emperor in the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 神策節度使衛伯玉攻史朝義，拔永寧，破澠池、福昌、長水等縣。

translations.literal: Shence military governor Wei Boyu attacked Shi Chaoyi, took Yongning, and broke Mianchi, Fuchang, Changshui, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Boyu of Shence defeated Chaoyi, capturing Yongning and several counties.

sentences.zh: 己酉，上朝獻太清宮；

translations.literal: On jiyou, the emperor attended court and offered at Taqing Palace;
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day the emperor worshipped at Taqing Palace;

sentences.zh: 庚戌，享太廟、元獻廟。

translations.literal: on gengxu, offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Yuanxian Temple.
translations.idiomatic: on gengxu at the ancestral and Yuanxian temples.

sentences.zh: 建丑月，辛亥朔，祀圜丘、太一壇。

translations.literal: Jianchou month, first day xinhai—sacrificed at the Round Altar and Grand Unity Altar.
translations.idiomatic: On the first xinhai day of jianchou month he sacrificed at the Round Altar and Grand Unity Altar.

sentences.zh: 平盧節度使侯希逸與范陽相攻連年，救援既絕，又為奚所侵，乃悉舉其軍二萬餘人襲李懷仙，破之，因引兵而南。

translations.literal: Pinglu military governor Hou Xiyi had battled Fanyang for years; relief was cut off and he was also invaded by the Xi—he therefore raised his entire army of more than twenty thousand to strike Li Huaixian, defeated him, and then led troops south.
translations.idiomatic: After years fighting Fanyang without relief and Xi raids, Hou Xiyi marched his twenty thousand men south, defeating Li Huaixian.

sentences.zh: 肅宗文明武德大聖大宣孝皇帝下之下寶應元年（

translations.literal: Below the second part of Emperor Suzong—the first year of Baoying (
translations.idiomatic: Continuing Emperor Suzong's reign—the first year of Baoying (

sentences.zh: 壬寅，公元七六二年）

translations.literal: renyin, CE 762)
translations.idiomatic: 762 CE, year renyin)

sentences.zh: 建丙月，甲申，追尊靖德太子琮為奉天皇帝，妃竇氏為恭應皇后，丁酉，葬於齊陵。

translations.literal: Jianbing month, on jiashen, posthumously honored Crown Prince Jingde Cong as Emperor Fengtian, consort Dou as Empress Gongying; on dingyou buried at Qiling.
translations.idiomatic: In jianbing month Prince Cong was posthumously enthroned as Emperor Fengtian and buried at Qiling on dingyou day.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，吐蕃遣使請和。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Tibet sent envoys requesting peace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day Tibet sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 李光弼拔許州，擒史朝義所署穎川太守李春；

translations.literal: Li Guangbi took Xuzhou and captured Yingchuan prefect Li Chun appointed by Shi Chaoyi;
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi took Xuzhou and captured Chaoyi's appointee Li Chun as Yingchuan prefect;

sentences.zh: 朝義將史參救之，丙午，戰於城下，又破之。

translations.literal: Chaoyi's general Shi Can came to rescue; on bingwu, they fought below the walls and Guangbi again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: General Shi Can's relief force was routed below the walls on bingwu day.

sentences.zh: 戊申，平盧節度使侯希逸於青州北渡河而會田神功、能元皓於兗州。

translations.literal: On wushen, Pinglu military governor Hou Xiyi north of Qingzhou crossed the river and joined Tian Shenggong and Neng Yuanhao at Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day Hou Xiyi crossed the Yellow River north of Qingzhou and joined Tian Shenggong and Neng Yuanhao at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 租庸使元載以江、淮雖經兵荒，其民比諸道猶有資產，乃按籍舉八年租調之違負及逋逃者，計其大數而征之；

translations.literal: Revenue commissioner Yuan Zai, though Jiang-Huai had passed through war and famine, held that its people compared with other circuits still had assets—he therefore according to registers cited eight years of rent and corvée defaults and fugitives, calculated the grand total and collected;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai decided that Jiang-Huai, despite war damage, still had wealth on the books and levied eight years of back taxes in lump sums;

sentences.zh: 擇豪吏為縣令而督之，不問負之有無，資之高下，察民有粟帛者發徒圍之，籍其所有而中分之，甚者什取八九，謂之白著。

translations.literal: chose fierce clerks as county magistrates to supervise—without asking whether debt existed or assets were high or low, when they saw people with grain or cloth they sent laborers to surround them, registered all they owned and split it in half—in severe cases taking eight or nine tenths—called "white levy."
translations.idiomatic: He sent harsh magistrates to seize grain and cloth, taking half—or eight or nine tenths in the worst cases—in the so-called "white levy."

sentences.zh: 有不服者，嚴刑以威之。

translations.literal: Those who did not submit were awed with severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Dissenters were crushed by torture.

sentences.zh: 民有蓄谷十斛者，則重足以待命，或相聚山澤為群盜，州縣不能制。

translations.literal: People who stored ten hu of grain braced their feet with heavy shackles awaiting orders; some gathered in mountains and marshes as bandit gangs—the prefectures and counties could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers with even ten hu of grain were shackled; others fled to the hills as bandits beyond county control.

sentences.zh: 建卯月，辛亥朔，赦天下；

translations.literal: Jianmao month, first day xinhai—amnestied the realm;
translations.idiomatic: On the first xinhai day of jianmao month the emperor amnestied the realm;

sentences.zh: 復以京兆為上都，河南為東都，鳳翔為西都，江陵為南都，太原為北都。

translations.literal: restored Jingzhao as Superior Capital, Henan as Eastern Capital, Fengxiang as Western Capital, Jiangling as Southern Capital, Taiyuan as Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: and restored the five capital designations.

sentences.zh: 奴剌寇成固。

translations.literal: Nula raided Chenggu.
translations.idiomatic: Nula raiders struck Chenggu.

sentences.zh: 初，王思禮為河東節度使，資儲豐衍，贍軍之外，積米百萬斛，奏請輸五十萬斛於京師。

translations.literal: Initially, Wang Sili was Hedong military governor—stores were abundant; beyond provisioning the army he accumulated a million hu of rice and memorialized to send five hundred thousand hu to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sili as Hedong governor had amassed a million hu of rice and offered half a million to the capital.

sentences.zh: 思禮薨，管崇嗣代之，為政寬弛，信任左右，數月間，耗散殆盡，惟陳腐米萬餘斛在。

translations.literal: Sili died; Guan Chongsi replaced him—his governance was lax, he trusted favorites, and within months stores were nearly exhausted—only more than ten thousand hu of stale rotten rice remained.
translations.idiomatic: After Sili's death Guan Chongsi squandered the granaries within months, leaving only rotten rice.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，以鄧景山代之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and replaced him with Deng Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Deng Jingshan to replace him.

sentences.zh: 景山至，則鉤校所出入，將士輩多有隱沒，皆懼。

translations.literal: When Jingshan arrived, he audited income and outgo—officers and soldiers mostly had much concealed embezzlement and all feared.
translations.idiomatic: Deng audited the books and frightened officers who had skimmed supplies.

sentences.zh: 有裨將抵罪當死，諸將請之，不許；

translations.literal: A staff general was guilty and deserved death—the generals pleaded for him, not granted;
translations.idiomatic: When a staff captain faced execution, his comrades pleaded in vain;

sentences.zh: 其弟請代兄死，亦不許；

translations.literal: his younger brother asked to die in his elder brother's place—also not granted;
translations.idiomatic: his brother offered to die in his stead and was refused;

sentences.zh: 請入一馬以贖死，乃許之。

translations.literal: asked to submit one horse to redeem death—then it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: only a horse ransom won a reprieve.

sentences.zh: 諸將怒曰：「我輩曾不及一馬乎！」

translations.literal: The generals angrily said, "We are not even worth one horse!"
translations.idiomatic: The officers fumed, "Are we worth less than a horse?"

sentences.zh: 遂作亂，癸丑，殺景山。

translations.literal: They then mutinied; on guichou they killed Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: They mutinied on guichou day and killed Deng Jingshan.

sentences.zh: 上以景山撫御失所以致亂，不復推究亂者，遣使慰諭以安之。

translations.literal: The emperor held that Jingshan's failure in soothing control had caused the mutiny and did not further investigate the mutineers—sent envoys to comfort and reassure to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed Deng's harshness, not the mutineers, and sent envoys to pacify the army.

sentences.zh: 諸將請以都知兵馬使、代州刺史辛雲京為節度使。

translations.literal: The generals requested that Chief of Staff and Daizhou prefect Xin Yunjing be made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: They demanded Xin Yunjing as the new governor.

sentences.zh: 己未，以雲京為北都留守、河東節度使。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Yunjing was made Northern Capital regent and Hedong military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day Xin Yunjing became regent of the northern capital and Hedong governor.

sentences.zh: 雲京奏張光晟為代州刺史。

translations.literal: Yunjing memorialized Zhang Guangcheng as Daizhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Zhang Guangcheng prefect of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 絳州素無儲蓄，民間饑，不可賦斂，將士糧賜不充，朔方等諸道行營都統李國貞屢以狀聞；

translations.literal: Jiangzhou had never had stores; the populace was famished—taxes could not be levied; officers' and soldiers' grain and rewards were insufficient—Shuofang and other circuit campaign overall commander Li Guozhen repeatedly reported in memorials;
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhou had no reserves, the people were starving, and pay ran short despite Li Guozhen's repeated memorials;

sentences.zh: 朝廷未報，軍中咨怨。

translations.literal: the court did not reply and the army murmured in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: the court did not respond and the troops grew mutinous.

sentences.zh: 突將王元振將作亂，矯令於眾曰：「來日修都統宅，各具畚鍤，待命於門。」

translations.literal: Strike general Wang Yuanzhen was about to mutiny; he falsely ordered the masses, saying, "Tomorrow repair the overall commander's residence—each bring hoe and basket, await orders at the gate."
translations.idiomatic: Strike captain Wang Yuanzhen plotted mutiny, falsely ordering the men to bring tools tomorrow to "repair the commander's house."

sentences.zh: 士卒皆怒，曰：「朔方健兒豈修宅夫邪！」

translations.literal: The soldiers were all angry, saying, "Shuofang stalwarts—are we house-repair laborers!"
translations.idiomatic: The Shuofang veterans roared that they were not construction workers.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，元振帥其徒作亂，燒牙城門。

translations.literal: On yichou, Yuanzhen led his followers in mutiny and burned the yamen gate.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day Yuanzhen mutinied and torched the headquarters gate.

sentences.zh: 國貞逃於獄，元振執之，置卒食於彰，曰：「食此而役其力，可乎？」

translations.literal: Guozhen fled into the prison; Yuanzhen seized him, set soldier rations before Zhang, and said, "Eat this and then labor with your strength—is that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen hid in the jail; Yuanzhen seized him and mocked, "Eat this ration, then work—is that fair?"

sentences.zh: 國貞曰：「修宅則無之，軍食則屢奏而未報，諸君所知也。」

translations.literal: Guozhen said, "House repair there is none; army rations I have repeatedly memorialized without reply—you all know this."
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen replied that no one had ordered house repairs and that grain requisitions went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 眾欲退。

translations.literal: The crowd wished to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The men began to disperse.

sentences.zh: 元振曰：「今日之事，何必更問！

translations.literal: Yuanzhen said, "Today's affair—why ask further!
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen shouted that there was nothing more to discuss.

sentences.zh: 都統不死，則我輩死矣。」

translations.literal: If the overall commander does not die, then we shall die."
translations.idiomatic: If the commander lives, we die."

sentences.zh: 遂拔刃殺之。

translations.literal: He then drew blade and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his sword and killed Guozhen.

sentences.zh: 鎮西、北庭行營兵屯於翼城，亦殺節度使荔非元禮，推裨將白孝德為節度使，朝廷因而授之。

translations.literal: "Zhenxi and Beiting campaign troops encamped at Yicheng also killed military governor Li Fei Yuanli, promoted staff general Bai Xiaode as military governor—the court thereupon appointed him.
translations.idiomatic: "At Yicheng, Zhenxi and Beiting troops killed governor Li Fei Yuanli and made Bai Xiaode governor, which the court confirmed.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，淮西節度使王仲升與史朝義將謝欽讓戰於申州城下，為賊所虜，淮西震駭。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Huaixi military governor Wang Zhongsheng fought Shi Chaoyi's general Xie Qinrang below Shenzhou walls and was captured by the rebels—Huaixi was shaken in terror.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day Wang Zhongsheng of Huaixi was captured fighting Xie Qinrang below Shenzhou, shocking the circuit.

sentences.zh: 會侯希逸、田神功、能元皓攻汴州，朝義召欽讓兵救之。

translations.literal: It happened that Hou Xiyi, Tian Shenggong, and Neng Yuanhao were attacking Bianzhou—Chaoyi summoned Qinrang's troops to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: As Hou Xiyi, Tian Shenggong, and Neng Yuanhao besieged Bianzhou, Chaoyi recalled Qinrang to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 絳州諸軍剽掠不已，朝廷憂其與太原亂軍合從連賊，非新進諸將所能鎮服，辛未，以郭子儀為汾陽王，知朔方、河中、北庭潞澤節度行營兼興平、定國等軍副元帥，發京師絹四萬匹、布五萬端、米六萬石以給絳軍。

translations.literal: The various Jiangzhou armies plundered without cease; the court feared they would ally with Taiyuan mutineers and link with rebels—not newly promoted generals could suppress them—on xinwei, Guo Ziyi was made Prince of Fenyang, given Shuofang, Hedong, Beiting, Lu-Ze campaign commands and concurrent Xingping and Dingguo armies deputy supreme commander; sent from the capital forty thousand bolts of silk, fifty thousand bolts of cloth, and sixty thousand shi of grain to supply the Jiangzhou army.
translations.idiomatic: With Jiangzhou troops looting and fearing alliance with Taiyuan mutineers, on xinwei day Guo Ziyi was made Prince of Fenyang and deputy commander, with huge supplies sent to Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 建辰月，庚寅，子儀將行，時上不豫，群臣莫得進見。

translations.literal: Jianchén month, on gengyin, Ziyi was about to depart—the emperor was unwell and ministers could not gain audience.
translations.idiomatic: In jianchén month, as Ziyi prepared to leave, the ailing emperor received no ministers.

sentences.zh: 子儀請曰：「老臣受命，將死於外，不見陛下，目不瞑矣！」

translations.literal: Ziyi requested, saying, "This old minister received the mandate and will die abroad—if I do not see Your Majesty, my eyes will not close in death!"
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi pleaded, "I may die on campaign without seeing you—my eyes would not close."

sentences.zh: 上召入臥內，謂曰：「河東之事，一以委卿。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him into the sickroom and said, "Hedong affairs—I wholly entrust to you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received him bedside and said, "All of Hedong is in your hands.

sentences.zh: 史朝義遣兵圍李抱玉於澤州，子儀發定國軍救之，乃去。

translations.literal: Shi Chaoyi sent troops to besiege Li Baoyu at Zezhou; Ziyi dispatched Dingguo army to rescue him, and they then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi besieged Li Baoyu at Zezhou until Ziyi sent the Dingguo army and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 上召山南東道節度使來瑱赴京師。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Shannan East Circuit military governor Lai Tian to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recalled Shannan East governor Lai Tian to court.

sentences.zh: 瑱樂在襄陽，其將士亦愛之，乃諷所部將吏上表留之，行及鄧州，復令還鎮。

translations.literal: Tian delighted in Xiangyang and his officers and soldiers also loved him—he therefore prompted his subordinate generals and officials to submit a memorial to retain him; when he reached Dengzhou, he was again ordered to return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Tian, beloved in Xiangyang, had his officers petition to keep him; at Dengzhou he was sent back.

sentences.zh: 荊南節度使呂諲、淮西節度使王仲升及中使往來者言：「瑱曲收眾心，恐久難制。」

translations.literal: Jingnan military governor Lü Yin, Huaixi military governor Wang Zhongsheng, and palace envoys coming and going said, "Tian by artifice gathers popular hearts—feared long difficult to control."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yin, Wang Zhongsheng, and envoys warned that Lai Tian was winning loyalty and would be hard to control.

sentences.zh: 上乃割商、金、均、房別置觀察使，令瑱止領六州。

translations.literal: The emperor then split off Shang, Jin, Jun, and Fang to establish a separate observation commissioner, ordering Tian to hold only six prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The court carved out four prefectures under a new observer and limited Lai Tian to six prefectures.

sentences.zh: 會謝欽讓圍王仲長升於申州數月，瑱怨之，按兵不救，仲升竟敗沒。

translations.literal: It happened that Xie Qinrang besieged Wang Zhongsheng at Shenzhou for months—Tian resented this and held troops without rescuing—Zhongsheng in the end was defeated and lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Qinrang besieged Wang Zhongsheng at Shenzhou for months, Lai Tian withheld aid and Wang fell.

sentences.zh: 行軍司馬裴□謀奪瑱位，密表瑱倔強難制，請以兵襲取之，上以為然。

translations.literal: Campaign army marshal Pei □ plotted to seize Tian's position, secretly memorialized that Tian was stubborn and hard to control, requested troops to seize him by surprise—the emperor thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Pei □ plotted to replace Lai Tian, urging a surprise arrest, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以瑱為淮西、河南十六州節度使，外示寵任，實欲圖之。

translations.literal: On guisi, Tian was made Huaixi and Henan sixteen-prefecture military governor—outwardly showing favor and trust, in reality intending to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day Lai Tian was promoted to a grand Huai-Henan command—a trap disguised as honor.

sentences.zh: 密敕以□代瑱為襄、鄧等州防禦使。

translations.literal: A secret edict made □ replace Tian as Xiang, Deng, and other prefectures defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Secret orders named Pei □ to replace him in Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 甲午，奴剌寇梁州，觀察使李勉棄城走，以邠州剌史河西臧希讓為山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Nula raided Liangzhou; observation commissioner Li Mian abandoned the city and fled—Binzhou prefect Hexi Zang Xirang was made Shannan West Circuit military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day Nula raided Liangzhou; Li Mian fled and Zang Xirang was named governor of Shannan West.

sentences.zh: 丙申，党項寇奉天。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Tangut raided Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day Tangut forces raided Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 李輔國以求宰相不得怨蕭華。

translations.literal: Li Fuguo, because seeking the chancellorship was not granted, resented Xiao Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuguo resented Xiao Hua after failing to become chancellor.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以戶部侍郎元載為京兆尹。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Hubu vice director Yuan Zai was made Jingzhao prefect.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day Yuan Zai became Jingzhao prefect.

sentences.zh: 載詣輔國固辭，輔國識其意；

translations.literal: Zai went to Fuguo and firmly declined; Fuguo understood his intent;
translations.idiomatic: Zai declined the post to Fuguo, who understood the gesture;

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以司農卿陶銳為京兆尹。

translations.literal: on renyin, Sinong Director Tao Rui was made Jingzhao prefect.
translations.idiomatic: on renyin Tao Rui of Sinong took the post instead.

sentences.zh: 輔國言蕭華專權，請罷其相，上不許。

translations.literal: Fuguo said Xiao Hua monopolized power and requested his removal from chancellor—the emperor did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo accused Xiao Hua of monopolizing power; the emperor refused to dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 輔國固請不已，乃從之，仍引元載代華。

translations.literal: Fuguo urgently requested without cease—the emperor then assented and still brought Yuan Zai to replace Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo kept pressing until the emperor agreed and Yuan Zai replaced Hua.

sentences.zh: 戊申，華罷為禮部尚書，以載同平章事，領度支、轉運如故。

translations.literal: On wushen, Hua was removed as Libu Minister; Zai was made fellow Grand Councillor, continuing to head revenue and transport as before.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day Xiao Hua became minister of rites while Yuan Zai joined the Grand Council and kept fiscal posts.

sentences.zh: 建巳月，庚戌朔，澤州剌史李抱玉破史朝義兵於城下。

translations.literal: Jiansi month, first day gengxu—Zezhou prefect Li Baoyu defeated Shi Chaoyi's troops below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: On the first gengxu day of jiansi month Li Baoyu routed Chaoyi's army at Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 壬子，楚州刺史崔侁表稱，有尼真如，恍惚登天，見上帝，賜以寶玉十三枚，云：「中國有災，以此鎮之。」

translations.literal: On renzi, Chuzhou prefect Cui Shen memorialized, saying there was a nun Zhenru who in a trance ascended heaven, saw the Supreme Emperor, and was granted thirteen pieces of precious jade, saying, "The Central State has disaster—use these to suppress it."
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhou prefect Cui Shen reported a nun who claimed a heavenly vision and thirteen jade talismans to ward off disaster.

sentences.zh: 群臣表賀。

translations.literal: The ministers submitted memorials of congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers sent congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，上皇崩於神龍殿，年七十八。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the Retired Emperor died in Shenlong Hall, age seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day the retired emperor died in Shenlong Hall at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，遷坐於太極殿。

translations.literal: On yimao, the coffin was moved to sit in Taiji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the bier was placed in Taiji Hall.

sentences.zh: 上以寢疾，發哀於內殿，群臣發哀於太極殿。

translations.literal: The emperor, being bedridden with illness, mourned in the inner hall; ministers mourned in Taiji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The ailing emperor mourned privately while officials mourned in Taiji Hall.

sentences.zh: 蕃官嫠面割耳者四百餘人。

translations.literal: More than four hundred foreign officials widows cut their faces and ears.
translations.idiomatic: Over four hundred foreign widows mutilated themselves in grief.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，命苗晉卿攝塚宰。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Miao Jinqing was ordered to act as chief mourner.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Miao Jinqing served as chief mourner.

sentences.zh: 上自仲春寢疾，聞上皇登遐，哀慕，疾轉劇，乃命太子監國。

translations.literal: The emperor since mid-spring had been bedridden; hearing the Retired Emperor had passed, he grieved and longed—illness turned severe—and he then ordered the Crown Prince to oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: Grief over his father's death worsened the emperor's illness and he named the crown prince regent.

sentences.zh: 甲子，制改元；

translations.literal: On jiazi, an edict changed the era name;
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day a new era was proclaimed;

sentences.zh: 復以建寅為正月，月數皆如其舊；

translations.literal: restored jianyin as first month, month numbers all as of old;
translations.idiomatic: restoring the normal calendar with jianyin as New Year;

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: and amnestied the realm.
translations.idiomatic: and amnestying the realm.

sentences.zh: 初，張後與李輔國相表裡，專權用事，晚年，更有隙。

translations.literal: Initially, Empress Zhang and Li Fuguo were mutually inside and outside, monopolizing power in affairs—in later years there was further rift.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang and Li Fuguo had once shared power but later fell out.

sentences.zh: 內射生使三原程元振黨於輔國。

translations.literal: Inner archer guard commissioner Sanyuan Cheng Yuanzhen sided with Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: Inner guard commissioner Cheng Yuanzhen backed Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 上疾篤，後召太子謂曰：「李輔國久典禁兵，制敕皆從之出，擅逼遷聖皇，其罪甚大，所忌者吾與太子。

translations.literal: The emperor's illness was grave; the empress summoned the Crown Prince and said, "Li Fuguo long controlled forbidden troops—all edicts issue from him; he on his own forced moving the Sage Emperor—his crime is very great; those he fears are me and the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On her deathbed the empress told the crown prince that Fuguo, who controlled the guards and had ousted the retired emperor, now threatened them both.

sentences.zh: 今主上彌留，輔國陰與程元振謀作亂，不可不誅。」

translations.literal: Now the sovereign lingers near death—Fuguo secretly with Cheng Yuanzhen plots rebellion—he must be executed."
translations.idiomatic: She urged killing Fuguo and Cheng Yuanzhen before they rebelled.

sentences.zh: 太子泣曰：「陛下疾甚危，二人皆陛下勳舊之臣，一日不告而誅之，必致震驚，恐不能堪也。」

translations.literal: The Crown Prince wept and said, "Your Majesty's illness is very perilous—both men are Your Majesty's meritorious old ministers; to execute them in one day without announcement would surely cause shock—I fear it cannot be borne."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince wept that executing two veteran ministers without warning would shock the court.

sentences.zh: 後曰：「然則太子姑歸，吾更徐思之。」

translations.literal: The empress said, "Then let the Crown Prince withdraw for now—I shall think further at leisure."
translations.idiomatic: The empress told him to leave while she reconsidered.

sentences.zh: 太子出，後召越王系謂曰：「太子仁弱，不能誅賊臣，汝能之乎？」

translations.literal: The Crown Prince left; the empress summoned Prince of Yue Xi and said, "The Crown Prince is benevolent and weak—he cannot execute villainous ministers; can you?"
translations.idiomatic: She then asked Prince Xi of Yue whether he could kill the traitors when the crown prince could not.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「能。」

translations.literal: He answered, "I can."
translations.idiomatic: He answered yes.

sentences.zh: 系乃命內謁者監段恆俊選宦官有勇力者二百餘人，授甲於長生殿後。

translations.literal: Xi then ordered Inner Usher Supervisor Duan Hengjun to select more than two hundred eunuchs with courage and strength, and armor was issued behind Longevity Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Xi armed over two hundred strong eunuchs behind Longevity Hall.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，後以上命召太子。

translations.literal: On yichou, the empress by imperial order summoned the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the empress summoned the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 元振知其謀，密告輔國，伏兵於陵霄門以俟之，太子至，以難告。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen knew the plot, secretly told Fuguo, and laid troops at Lingxiao Gate to await—the Crown Prince arrived and was told of the danger.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen tipped off Fuguo, who ambushed Lingxiao Gate and warned the prince.

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「必無是事。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince said, "Surely there is no such affair.
translations.idiomatic: The prince insisted there was no plot.

sentences.zh: 主上疾，亟召我，我豈可畏死而不赴乎！」

translations.literal: The sovereign is ill and urgently summons me—how could I fear death and not go!"
translations.idiomatic: Father is ill and calls me—I cannot refuse out of fear!"

sentences.zh: 元振曰：「社稷事大，太子必不可入。」

translations.literal: Yuanzhen said, "The altars of soil and grain are a great matter—the Crown Prince absolutely must not enter."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen said the realm came first and barred him from entering.

sentences.zh: 乃以兵送太子於飛龍廄，且以甲卒守之。

translations.literal: He then with troops escorted the Crown Prince to Flying Dragon Stable and also stationed armored soldiers to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Troops escorted him to Flying Dragon Stable under guard.

sentences.zh: 是夜，輔國、元振勒兵三殿，收捕越王系、段恆俊及知內侍省事朱光輝等百餘人，系之。

translations.literal: That night Fuguo and Yuanzhen mustered troops in the Three Halls, seized Prince of Yue Xi, Duan Hengjun, and Director of Palace Domestic Service Zhu Guanghui and more than a hundred others, and bound them.
translations.idiomatic: That night Fuguo and Yuanzhen seized Prince Xi, Duan Hengjun, Zhu Guanghui, and over a hundred others.

sentences.zh: 以太子之命遷後於別殿。

translations.literal: By the Crown Prince's order the empress was moved to a separate hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the prince's order the empress was moved to another hall.

sentences.zh: 時上在長生殿，使者逼後下殿，並左右數十人幽於後宮，宦官宮人皆驚駭逃散。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was in Longevity Hall; envoys forced the empress down from the hall, and several tens of attendants were confined in the rear palace—eunuchs and palace women all fled in shock.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys dragged the empress away while attendants were confined; palace staff fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，上崩。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 輔國等殺後並系及兗王僩。

translations.literal: Fuguo and company killed the empress together with Xi and Prince of Yan Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo killed the empress, Prince Xi, and Prince Qian of Yan.

sentences.zh: 是日，輔國始引太子素服於九仙門與宰相相見，敘上皇晏駕，拜哭，始行監國之令。

translations.literal: That day Fuguo first led the Crown Prince in plain garb at Jiuxian Gate to meet chancellors, narrated the Retired Emperor's passing, bowed and wept, and began executing regency orders.
translations.idiomatic: That day Fuguo brought the prince in mourning to meet the chancellors and begin regency.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，發大行皇帝喪於兩儀殿，宣遺詔。

translations.literal: On wuchen, the late emperor's mourning was proclaimed at Liangyi Hall and the testamentary edict was announced.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the late emperor's mourning was proclaimed and the will read.

sentences.zh: 己巳，代宗即位。

translations.literal: On jisi, Emperor Daizong took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Emperor Daizong ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 高力士遇赦還，至朗州，聞上皇崩，號慟，嘔血而卒。

translations.literal: Gao Lishi, meeting amnesty, returned; reaching Langzhou he heard the Retired Emperor had died—wailed in grief, vomited blood, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi, pardoned and returning, died of grief at Langzhou on hearing of the retired emperor's death.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以皇子奉節王適為天下兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, imperial son Prince of Fengjie Shi was made overall commander of all armies and horses under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day Prince Shi of Fengjie was named supreme commander of all armies.

sentences.zh: 李輔國恃功益橫，明謂上曰：「大家但居禁中，外事聽老奴處分。」

translations.literal: Li Fuguo relying on merit grew more overbearing, openly telling the emperor, "Your Majesty need only dwell in the inner palace—outer affairs leave to this old slave to dispose."
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo boasted to the emperor, "Stay in the palace; leave outside affairs to me."

sentences.zh: 上內不能平，以其方握禁兵，外尊禮之。

translations.literal: The emperor inwardly could not be at peace, but because Fuguo then held forbidden troops, outwardly honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong inwardly seethed but outwardly honored him while he held the guards.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，號輔國為尚父而不名，事無大小皆咨之，群臣出入皆先詣，輔國亦晏然處之。

translations.literal: On yihai, Fuguo was titled Imperial Father without naming him—all affairs great and small were consulted with him; ministers entering and leaving all first visited him—Fuguo also calmly accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day Fuguo was styled Imperial Father; ministers paid court to him first.

sentences.zh: 以內飛龍廄副使程元振為左監門衛將軍。

translations.literal: Inner Flying Dragon Stable deputy Cheng Yuanzhen was made Left Gate Guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanzhen became Left Gate Guard general.

sentences.zh: 知內侍省事朱光輝及內常侍啖庭瑤、山人李唐等二十餘人皆流黔中。

translations.literal: Director of Palace Domestic Service Zhu Guanghui and Inner Regular Attendant Dan Tingyao, mountain man Li Tang, and more than twenty others were all exiled to Qianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Guanghui, Dan Tingyao, Li Tang, and over twenty others were exiled to Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 初，李國貞治軍嚴，朔方將士不樂，皆思郭子儀，故王元振因之作亂。

translations.literal: Initially, Li Guozhen governed the army strictly—the Shuofang officers and soldiers were displeased, all longed for Guo Ziyi; hence Wang Yuanzhen took advantage to mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guozhen's harsh discipline made Shuofang troops long for Guo Ziyi, enabling Yuanzhen's mutiny.

sentences.zh: 子儀至軍，元振自以為功，子儀曰：「汝臨賊境，輒害主將，若賊乘其釁，無絳州矣。

translations.literal: Ziyi reached the army; Yuanzhen considered himself meritorious—Ziyi said, "You faced the enemy border yet rashly harmed the chief commander—if rebels seized that opening, there would be no Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi rebuked Yuanzhen for killing his commander on the frontier and inviting enemy attack.

sentences.zh: 吾為宰相，豈受一卒之私邪！」

translations.literal: I serve as chancellor—how would I accept one soldier's private favor!"
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor, I will not show favor to one soldier."

sentences.zh: 五月，庚辰，收元振及其同謀四十人，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on gengchen, Yuanzhen and his forty fellow conspirators were seized—all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on gengchen day, Yuanzhen and forty conspirators were executed.

sentences.zh: 辛雲京聞之，亦推按鄧景山者數十人，誅之。

translations.literal: Xin Yunjing heard of it and also investigated several tens involved with Deng Jingshan and executed them.
