translations.idiomatic: Xin Yunjing likewise executed dozens tied to Deng Jingshan's murder.

sentences.zh: 由是河東諸鎮率皆奉法。

translations.literal: Henceforth Hedong garrisons mostly all obeyed the law.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong garrisons thereafter mostly obeyed the law.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以李輔國為司空兼中書令。

translations.literal: On renwu, Li Fuguo was made Minister of Works concurrent Zhongshu Director.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day Li Fuguo was made minister of works and director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 党項寇同官、華原。

translations.literal: Tangut raided Tongguan and Huayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tangut raiders struck Tongguan and Huayuan.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以平盧節度使侯希逸為平盧、青、淄等六州節度使，由是青州節度有平盧之號。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Pinglu military governor Hou Xiyi was made Pinglu, Qing, Zi, and other six-prefecture military governor—henceforth Qingzhou governorship bore the Pinglu title.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day Hou Xiyi received the six-prefecture Pinglu command, giving Qingzhou the Pinglu name.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，徙奉節王適為魯王。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Prince of Fengjie Shi was transferred to Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shi of Fengjie was retitled Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，追尊上母吳妃為皇太后。

translations.literal: On gengyin, the emperor's mother Consort Wu was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin the emperor's mother Lady Wu was posthumously made empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，貶禮部尚書蕭華為峽州司馬。

translations.literal: On renchen, Libu Minister Xiao Hua was demoted to Xiachzhou staff administrator.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Xiao Hua was demoted to staff administrator of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 元載希李輔國意，以罪誣之也。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai hoping to please Li Fuguo falsely accused him by crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai framed him to please Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 敕乾元大小錢皆一當一，民始安之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Qianyuan large and small coin both one for one—the people then first settled in peace.
translations.idiomatic: An edict fixed Qianyuan coins at par, easing popular distress.

sentences.zh: 史朝義自圍宋州數月，城中食盡，將陷，剌史李岑不知所為。

translations.literal: Shi Chaoyi himself besieged Songzhou for months; food in the city was exhausted and it was about to fall—prefect Li Cen did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: After months besieging Songzhou until food ran out, Prefect Li Cen despaired.

sentences.zh: 遂城果毅開封劉昌曰：「倉中猶有麴數千斤，請屑食之；

translations.literal: Suicheng guard officer Kaifeng Liu Chang said, "In the granary there are still several thousand jin of yeast mash—please crumble and eat it;
translations.idiomatic: Guard officer Liu Chang of Kaifeng proposed eating leftover mash from the stores;

sentences.zh: 不過二十日，李太尉必救我。

translations.literal: within twenty days Grand Marshal Li will surely rescue us.
translations.idiomatic: within twenty days Marshal Li Guangbi would relieve them.

sentences.zh: 城東南隅最危，昌請守之。」

translations.literal: The southeast corner of the wall is most perilous—I request to defend it."
translations.idiomatic: He volunteered to hold the most threatened southeast corner.

sentences.zh: 李光弼至臨淮，諸將以朝義兵尚強，請南保揚州。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi reached Linhuai; generals, because Chaoyi's troops were still strong, requested south to secure Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Linhuai, generals urged retreat to Yangzhou while Chaoyi remained strong.

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「朝廷倚我以為安危，我復退縮，朝廷何望！

translations.literal: Guangbi said, "The court relies on me for safety and peril—if I again shrink back, what hope has the court!
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi refused: "The court trusts me for its safety—I cannot retreat.

sentences.zh: 且吾出其不意，賊安知吾之眾寡！」

translations.literal: Moreover we strike where they do not expect—how would rebels know our numbers!"
translations.idiomatic: A surprise move will hide our numbers."

sentences.zh: 遂徑趣徐州，使兗鄆節度使田神功進擊朝義，大破之。

translations.literal: He then went straight to Xuzhou, had Yan-Yun military governor Tian Shenggong advance to attack Chaoyi, and greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Xuzhou and had Tian Shenggong crush Chaoyi's force.

sentences.zh: 先是，田神功既克劉展，留連揚州未還，太子賓客尚衡與左羽林大將軍殷仲卿相攻於兗、鄆，聞光弼至，憚其威名，神功遽還河南，衡、仲卿相繼入朝。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tian Shenggong having defeated Liu Zhan lingered at Yangzhou and did not return—Crown Prince guest Shang Heng and Left Yulin Grand General Yin Zhongqing mutually attacked in Yan and Yun; hearing Guangbi had arrived, they feared his martial fame—Shenggong hastily returned to Henan, and Heng and Zhongqing successively entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tian Shenggong had lingered in Yangzhou; Shang Heng and Yin Zhongqing fought in Yan-Yun until Guangbi's arrival sent Tian back and both rivals to court.

sentences.zh: 光弼在徐州，惟軍旅之事自決之，自餘眾務，悉委判官張參。

translations.literal: Guangbi at Xuzhou decided military affairs alone; all other numerous duties he wholly entrusted to aide Zhang Can.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuzhou Guangbi kept military command while delegate Zhang Can ran everything else.

sentences.zh: 參吏事精敏，區處如流，諸將白事，光弼多令與參議之，諸將事如光弼，由是軍中肅然，東夏以寧。

translations.literal: Can was sharp in clerical affairs and disposed matters like flowing water; when generals reported affairs Guangbi often had them discuss with Can—generals handled matters as Guangbi did—hence the army was solemn and east Xia was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Can ran staff work with ease; generals routed business through him as Guangbi did, and order returned to the east.

sentences.zh: 先是，田神功起偏裨為節度使，留前使判官劉位等於幕府，神功皆平受其拜；

translations.literal: Earlier, Tian Shenggong rose from staff officer to military governor and kept former governor aide Liu Wei and others in the staff office—Shenggong all equally accepted their bows;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Shenggong, risen from the ranks, had kept former aides like Liu Wei who still bowed to him as equals;

sentences.zh: 及見光弼與參抗禮，乃大驚，遍拜位等曰：「神功出於行伍，不知禮儀，諸君亦胡為不言，成神功之過乎！」

translations.literal: When he saw Guangbi and Can treat each other as equals, he was greatly shocked and bowed all around to Wei and company, saying, "Shenggong came from the ranks and does not know ritual—why did you gentlemen also not speak and complete Shenggong's fault!"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Guangbi treat Zhang Can as an equal shocked Tian, who apologized to his staff for his own ignorance of etiquette;"

sentences.zh: 丁酉，赦天下。

translations.literal: On dingyou, amnestied the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day the court amnestied the realm.

sentences.zh: 立皇子益昌王邈為鄭王，延為慶王，迥為韓王。

translations.literal: Imperial sons Prince of Yichang Miao was installed as Prince of Zheng, Yan as Prince of Qing, and Jiong as Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Miao, Yan, and Jiong were enfeoffed as Princes of Zheng, Qing, and Han.

sentences.zh: 來瑱聞徙淮西，大懼，上言：「淮西無糧，請俟收麥而行。」

translations.literal: Lai Tian heard of transfer to Huaixi and was greatly afraid; he submitted, saying, "Huaixi has no grain—please wait until wheat harvest before marching."
translations.idiomatic: Lai Tian, terrified of transfer to Huaixi, asked to delay until the wheat harvest;

sentences.zh: 又諷將吏留己。

translations.literal: He also prompted officers and officials to retain him.
translations.idiomatic: he also had his officers petition to keep him.

sentences.zh: 上欲姑息無事，壬寅，復以瑱為山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to appease and avoid trouble; on renyin, Tian was again made Shannan East Circuit military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking peace, on renyin day the emperor restored Lai Tian to Shannan East.

sentences.zh: 飛龍副使程元振謀奪李輔國權，密言於上，請稍加裁製。

translations.literal: Flying Dragon deputy Cheng Yuanzhen plotted to seize Li Fuguo's power, secretly spoke to the emperor, and requested slight restraint and regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanzhen plotted against Fuguo and urged the emperor to rein him in.

sentences.zh: 六月，己未，解輔國行軍司馬及兵部尚書，餘如故，以元振代判元帥行軍司馬，仍遷輔國出居外第。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on jiwei, removed Fuguo as campaign army marshal and Minister of War—the rest as before; Yuanzhen replaced him as acting supreme commander campaign marshal, and Fuguo was still moved out to dwell at an outer residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiwei day, Fuguo lost his marshal and war ministry posts; Yuanzhen replaced him and Fuguo was moved out of the palace.

sentences.zh: 於是道路相賀。

translations.literal: Thereupon people congratulated one another on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: People celebrated in the streets.

sentences.zh: 輔國始懼，上表遜位。

translations.literal: Fuguo first grew afraid and submitted a memorial yielding his position.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo, alarmed, offered to resign.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，罷輔國兼中書令，進爵博陸王。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Fuguo was removed as concurrent Zhongshu Director and advanced in rank to Prince of Bolu.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day he lost the Secretariat post but was made Prince of Bolu.

sentences.zh: 輔國入謝，憤咽而言曰：「老奴事郎君不了，請歸地下事先帝！」

translations.literal: Fuguo entered to thank, speaking with choked rage: "This old slave could not serve Your Majesty to completion—please let me return below ground to serve the late emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo visited court choking with rage, saying he had failed the emperor and wished to join the late emperor in death.

sentences.zh: 上猶慰諭而遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor still comforted and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以兵部侍郎嚴武為西川節度使。

translations.literal: On renxu, Hubu vice director Yan Wu was made Xichuan military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day Yan Wu became Xichuan governor.

sentences.zh: 襄鄧防禦使裴谷屯穀城，既得密敕，即帥麾下二千人沿漢趣襄陽；

translations.literal: Xiang-Deng defense commissioner Pei Gu encamped at Gucheng; having received the secret edict, he immediately led two thousand under his command along the Han toward Xiangyang;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gu at Gucheng marched two thousand men down the Han toward Xiangyang on secret orders;

sentences.zh: 己巳，陳於谷水北。

translations.literal: On jisi, he arrayed north of the Gushui River.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day he formed up north of the Gushui.

sentences.zh: 瑱以兵逆之，問其所以來，對曰：「尚書不不受朝命，故來。

translations.literal: Tian met him with troops, asking why he came; he answered, "Your Excellency did not refuse the court's order—therefore we came.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Tian confronted him; Pei said he came because Lai Tian had not obeyed the transfer order.

sentences.zh: 若受代，謹當釋兵。」

translations.literal: If you accept replacement, we respectfully release arms."
translations.idiomatic: If you accept replacement, we will stand down."

sentences.zh: 瑱曰：「吾已蒙恩，復留鎮此，何受代之有！」

translations.literal: Tian said, "I have already received grace and again remain to guard here—what replacement is there!"
translations.idiomatic: Lai Tian said he had been graciously allowed to stay—there was no replacement.

sentences.zh: 因取敕及告身示之，瑱驚惑。

translations.literal: He then took out the edict and commission and showed them—Tian was shocked and confused.
translations.idiomatic: He produced the edict and commission, leaving Lai Tian stunned.

sentences.zh: 瑱與副使薛南陽縱兵夾擊，大破之，追擒□於申口，送京師；

translations.literal: Tian with deputy Xue Nanyang unleashed troops in pincer attack and greatly defeated them, pursued and captured □ at Shenkou, and sent him to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Lai Tian and Xue Nanyang crushed Pei's force, captured □ at Shenkou, and sent him to the capital;

sentences.zh: 賜死。

translations.literal: He was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: He was executed by imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以通州刺史劉晏為戶部侍郎兼京兆尹，充度支、轉運、鹽鐵、鑄錢等使。

translations.literal: On yihai, Tongzhou prefect Liu Yan was made Hubu vice director concurrent Jingzhao prefect, charged with revenue, transport, salt and iron, coinage, and other commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day Liu Yan became vice minister of revenue, Jingzhao prefect, and fiscal commissioner.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬辰，以郭子儀都知朔方、河東、北庭、潞、儀、澤、沁、陳、鄭等節度行營及興平等軍副元帥。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on renchen, Guo Ziyi was given overall command of Shuofang, Hedong, Beiting, Lu, Yi, Ze, Qin, Chen, Zheng and other circuit campaign armies and Xingping and other armies deputy supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Guo Ziyi was placed over Shuofang, Hedong, and allied commands as deputy supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，劍南兵馬使徐知道反，以兵守要害，拒嚴武，武不得進。

translations.literal: On guisi, Jiannan army horse commissioner Xu Zhidao rebelled, held troops at strategic points, blocked Yan Wu—Wu could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day Xu Zhidao rebelled in Jiannan and blocked Yan Wu's advance.

sentences.zh: 八月，桂州刺史刑濟討西原賊帥吳功曹等，平之。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Guizhou prefect Xing Ji attacked Western Plain bandit chiefs Wu Gongcao and others and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Xing Ji of Guizhou suppressed bandits under Wu Gongcao.

sentences.zh: 己未，徐知道為其將李忠勇所殺，劍南悉平。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Xu Zhidao was killed by his general Li Zhongyong—Jiannan was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day Li Zhongyong killed Xu Zhidao and Jiannan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，山南東道節度使瑱入朝謝罪，上優待之。

translations.literal: On yichou, Shannan East military governor Tian entered court to confess guilt—the emperor treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day Lai Tian submitted to court and was treated leniently.

sentences.zh: 己巳，郭子儀自河東入朝。

translations.literal: On jisi, Guo Ziyi from Hedong entered court.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day Guo Ziyi came to court from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 時程元振用事，忌子儀功高任重，數譖之於上。

translations.literal: At that time Cheng Yuanzhen held power, envied Ziyi's high merit and heavy responsibility, and repeatedly slandered him to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanzhen, jealous of Guo Ziyi's stature, slandered him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 子儀不自安，表請解副元帥、節度使。

translations.literal: Ziyi was not at ease and memorialized requesting release from deputy supreme commander and military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi, uneasy, asked to resign his commands.

sentences.zh: 上慰撫之，子儀遂留京師。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him—Ziyi then remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reassured him and he stayed at court.

sentences.zh: 台州賊帥袁晁攻陷浙東諸州，改元寶勝；

translations.literal: Taizhou bandit chief Yuan Chao attacked and captured Zhedong prefectures, changed era name to Baosheng;
translations.idiomatic: Bandit Yuan Chao seized Zhedong prefectures and proclaimed the era Baosheng;

sentences.zh: 民疲於賦斂者多歸之。

translations.literal: people weary of levies mostly joined him.
translations.idiomatic: tax-weary commoners flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 李光弼遣兵擊晁於衢州，破之。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi sent troops to strike Chao at Quzhou and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi defeated Yuan Chao at Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，徙魯王適為雍王。

translations.literal: On yihai, Prince of Lu Shi was transferred to Prince of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shi of Lu was retitled Prince of Yong.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚辰，以來瑱為兵部尚書、同平章事、知山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on gengchen, Lai Tian was made Hubu Minister, fellow Grand Councillor, and acting Shannan East military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Lai Tian joined the Grand Council as minister of war while keeping Shannan East.

sentences.zh: 乙未，加程元振驃騎大將軍兼內侍監。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Cheng Yuanzhen was added Flying Cavalry Grand General concurrent Palace Domestic Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day Cheng Yuanzhen was made flying cavalry grand general and palace supervisor.

sentences.zh: 左僕射裴冕為山陵使，議事有與程元振相違者，丙申，貶冕施州刺史。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Pei Mian was mausoleum commissioner; when deliberations differed from Cheng Yuanzhen, on bingchen Mian was demoted to Shizhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mian, clashing with Cheng Yuanzhen over the imperial tomb, was exiled to Shizhou on bingchen day.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使劉清潭使於回紇，修舊好，且徵兵討史朝義。

translations.literal: The emperor sent palace envoy Liu Qingtan as envoy to the Uyghurs to restore old friendship and also summon troops to attack Shi Chaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Liu Qingtan to the Uyghurs to renew alliance and seek troops against Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 清潭至其庭，回紇登裡可汗已為朝義所誘，云「唐室繼有大喪，今中原無主，可汗宜速來共收其府庫。」

translations.literal: When Qingtan reached their court, Uyghur Tengri Qaghan had already been enticed by Chaoyi, saying, "The Tang house has successive great mourning—now the central plain has no master—the Qaghan should quickly come and together seize their treasuries."
translations.idiomatic: At the Uyghur court Chaoyi's agents told the qaghan the Tang throne was empty and invited him to seize its treasuries.

sentences.zh: 可汗信之。

translations.literal: The Qaghan believed it.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan believed them.

sentences.zh: 清潭致敕書曰：「先帝雖棄天下，今上繼統，乃昔日廣平王，與葉護共收兩京者也。」

translations.literal: Qingtan delivered the imperial letter saying, "Though the late emperor abandoned the realm, the present sovereign succeeds—the former Prince of Guangping, who with Yabghu jointly recovered the two capitals."
translations.idiomatic: Qingtan presented the edict noting the new emperor was the Prince of Guangping who had retaken the capitals with the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 回紇業已起兵至三城，見州、縣皆為丘墟，有輕唐之志，乃困辱清潭。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs having already raised troops to Sancheng, saw prefectures and counties all ruins, had mind to slight Tang, and therefore humiliated Qingtan.
translations.idiomatic: Marching to Sancheng and seeing Tang lands in ruins, they despised the Tang and abused Qingtan.

sentences.zh: 清潭遣使言狀，且曰：「回紇舉國十萬眾至矣！」

translations.literal: Qingtan sent envoys reporting the situation, also saying, "The Uyghurs have raised the whole nation—a hundred thousand have arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: Qingtan warned that a hundred thousand Uyghurs were coming.

sentences.zh: 京師大駭。

translations.literal: The capital was greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: The capital panicked.

sentences.zh: 上遣殿中監藥子昂往勞之於忻州南。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Palace Supervisor Yao Ziang to greet them south of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yao Ziang to greet them south of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，毘伽闕可汗為登裡求婚，肅宗以僕固懷恩女妻之，為登裡可敦，可汗請與懷恩相見，懷恩時在汾州，上令往見之，懷恩為可汗言唐家恩信不可負，可汗悅，遣使上表，請助國討朝義。

translations.literal: Initially, Qaghan Mojilian sought marriage for Tengri—Suzong gave Pugu Huai'en's daughter as Tengri Khatun; the Qaghan requested to meet Huai'en; Huai'en was then at Fenzhou—the emperor ordered him to go meet; Huai'en told the Qaghan Tang grace and faith must not be betrayed—the Qaghan was pleased and sent envoys with memorial requesting to aid the state against Chaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Mojilian had married Huai'en's daughter to Tengri; Huai'en persuaded the qaghan to honor Tang and help fight Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 可汗欲自蒲關入，由沙苑出潼關東向，藥子昂說之曰：「關中數遭兵荒，州縣蕭條，無以供擬，恐可汗失望；

translations.literal: The Qaghan wished to enter by Puguan Pass, exit Tong Pass eastward via Sha Garden—Yao Ziang persuaded him, saying, "Guanzhong has repeatedly suffered war and famine—prefectures and counties are desolate, nothing to supply provisions—I fear the Qaghan will be disappointed;
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan wanted to enter via Puguan and Tong Pass; Yao Ziang warned that ravaged Guanzhong could not feed his army;

sentences.zh: 賊兵盡在洛陽，請自土門略邢、洺、懷、衛而南，得其資財以充軍裝。」

translations.literal: rebels are all at Luoyang—please from Tumen cross Xing, Ming, Huai, and Wei southward and take their wealth to fill army equipage."
translations.idiomatic: he urged a southern route through Xing and Ming to loot rebel-held wealth for supplies.

sentences.zh: 可汗不從；

translations.literal: The Qaghan did not follow;
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan refused;

sentences.zh: 又請「自太行南下據河陰，扼賊咽喉」，亦不從；

translations.literal: again requested "from Taihang south to hold Heyin and choke the rebels' throat"—also not followed;
translations.idiomatic: a plan to seize Heyin via the Taihang was also rejected;

sentences.zh: 又請「自陝州大陽津渡河，食太原倉粟，與諸道俱進」，乃從之。

translations.literal: again requested "from Shaanzhou cross at Dayang Ford, eat Taiyuan granary grain, advance together with all circuits"—then he followed.
translations.idiomatic: only when Yao proposed crossing at Dayang Ford to use Taiyuan grain did the qaghan agree.

sentences.zh: 袁晁陷信州。

translations.literal: Yuan Chao captured Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chao captured Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，袁晁陷溫州、明州。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, Yuan Chao captured Wenzhou and Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Yuan Chao took Wenzhou and Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以雍王適為天下兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: Prince of Yong Shi was made overall commander of armies and horses under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shi of Yong was named supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，辭行，以兼御史中丞藥子昂、魏琚為左、右廂兵馬使，以中書舍人韋少華為判官，給事中李進為行軍司馬，會諸道節度使及回紇於陝州，進討史朝義。

translations.literal: On xinyou, taking leave to depart—Concurrent Censor-in-Chief Yao Ziang and Wei Ju were left and right wing army horse commissioners; Zhongshu drafting officer Wei Shaohua was aide; Palace Attendant Li Jin was campaign marshal—they assembled circuit governors and Uyghurs at Shaanzhou to advance against Shi Chaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day the prince set out with Yao Ziang and Wei Ju as wing commanders, assembling allies at Shaanzhou against Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 上欲以郭子儀為適副，程元振、魚朝恩等沮之而止。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make Guo Ziyi the prince's deputy—Cheng Yuanzhen, Yu Chao'en, and others obstructed and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted Guo Ziyi as deputy but Cheng Yuanzhen and Yu Chao'en blocked it.

sentences.zh: 加朔方節度使僕固懷恩同平章事兼絳州刺史，領諸軍節度行營以副適。

translations.literal: Added Shuofang military governor Pugu Huai'en as fellow Grand Councillor concurrent Jiangzhou prefect, leading various armies campaign headquarters as deputy to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en was made grand councillor and deputy commander under the prince.

sentences.zh: 上在東宮，以李輔國專橫，心甚不平，及嗣位，以輔國有殺張後之功，不欲顯誅之。

translations.literal: When the emperor was in the Eastern Palace he resented Li Fuguo's monopoly and overbearing conduct; on succeeding the throne, because Fuguo had merit in killing Empress Zhang, he did not wish to execute him openly.
translations.idiomatic: As crown prince Daizong had hated Fuguo's arrogance but spared him openly for killing Empress Zhang.

sentences.zh: 壬戌夜，盜入其第，竊輔國之首及一臂而去。

translations.literal: On the night of renxu, thieves entered his residence, stole Fuguo's head and one arm, and left.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu night thieves beheaded Fuguo and took an arm.

sentences.zh: 敕有司捕盜，遣中使存問其家，為刻木首葬之，仍贈太傅。

translations.literal: An edict ordered officials to capture the thieves; sent palace envoys to inquire after his family, carved a wooden head for burial, and still posthumously granted Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The court hunted the killers, buried a wooden head, and posthumously made him grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，上命僕固懷恩與母、妻俱詣行營。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the emperor ordered Pugu Huai'en with mother and wife all to go to the campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day Huai'en was ordered to bring his mother and wife to camp.

sentences.zh: 雍王適至陝州，回紇可汗屯於河北，適與僚屬從數十騎往見之。

translations.literal: Prince of Yong Shi reached Shaanzhou; the Uyghur Qaghan encamped north of the river—Shi with staff followed by several dozen horsemen went to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shi rode with a small escort to visit the Uyghur qaghan north of the river.

sentences.zh: 可汗責適不拜舞，藥子昂對以禮不當然。

translations.literal: The Qaghan reproached Shi for not bowing in dance—Yao Ziang replied that ritual did not require it.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan demanded obeisance; Yao Ziang said protocol did not require it.

sentences.zh: 回紇將軍車鼻曰：「唐天子與可汗約為兄弟，可汗於雍王，叔父也，何得不拜舞」子昂曰：「雍王，天子長子，今為元帥。

translations.literal: Uyghur general Chebi said, "The Tang Son of Heaven and the Qaghan agreed as brothers—the Qaghan to the Prince of Yong is uncle—how can he not bow in dance!" Ziang said, "The Prince of Yong is the Son of Heaven's eldest son, now supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: General Chebi insisted the prince must bow as nephew; Yao Ziang replied he was the heir and commander.

sentences.zh: 安有中國儲君向外國可汗拜舞乎！」

translations.literal: How could there be the Central State's heir apparent bowing in dance to a foreign Qaghan!"
translations.idiomatic: How could a Tang crown prince prostrate to a foreign qaghan!"

sentences.zh: 且兩宮在殯，不應舞蹈。」

translations.literal: Moreover both palaces are in mourning—one should not dance in obeisance."
translations.idiomatic: With both emperors' coffins in mourning, dancing obeisance was improper."

sentences.zh: 力爭久之，車鼻遂引子昂、魏琚、韋少華、李進各鞭一百，以適年少未諳事，遣歸營。

translations.literal: After long forceful dispute, Chebi then had Ziang, Wei Ju, Wei Shaohua, and Li Jin each whipped a hundred times; because Shi was young and not versed in affairs, sent back to camp.
translations.idiomatic: After heated argument Chebi had Yao Ziang, Wei Ju, Wei Shaohua, and Li Jin flogged a hundred strokes each and sent the young prince back to camp.

sentences.zh: 琚、少華一夕而死。

translations.literal: Ju and Shaohua died within the night.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ju and Wei Shaohua died that night.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，諸軍發陝州，僕固懷恩與回紇左殺為前鋒，陝西節度使郭英乂、神策觀軍容使魚朝恩為殿，自澠池入；

translations.literal: On wuchen, all armies departed Shaanzhou—Pugu Huai'en with Uyghur Left Kill as vanguard, Shaanxi military governor Guo Yingyi and Shence army-inspection commissioner Yu Chao'en as rear guard, entering from Mianchi;
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the allied armies left Shaanzhou with Huai'en and Uyghur vanguard, Guo Yingyi and Yu Chao'en in the rear, via Mianchi;

sentences.zh: 潞澤節度使李抱玉自河陽入；

translations.literal: Lu-Ze military governor Li Baoyu entered from Heyang;
translations.idiomatic: Li Baoyu entered from Heyang;

sentences.zh: 河南等道副元帥李光弼自陳留入；

translations.literal: Henan and other circuits deputy supreme commander Li Guangbi entered from Chenliu;
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi advanced from Chenliu;

sentences.zh: 雍王留陝州。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yong remained at Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shi stayed at Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛未，懷恩等軍於同軌。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Huai'en and company encamped at Tonggui.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day Huai'en camped at Tonggui.

sentences.zh: 史朝義聞官軍將至，謀於諸將。

translations.literal: Shi Chaoyi heard government armies were about to arrive and consulted the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi consulted his generals as imperial troops approached.

sentences.zh: 阿史那承慶曰：「唐若獨與漢兵來，宜悉眾與戰；

translations.literal: Ashina Chengqing said, "If Tang comes only with Han troops, we should gather all forces and fight;
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Chengqing advised fighting if the Tang came alone, but retreating if Uyghurs joined;

sentences.zh: 若與回紇俱來，其鋒不可當，宜退守河陽以避之。」

translations.literal: if they come together with the Uyghurs, their edge cannot be withstood—we should withdraw to guard Heyang and avoid them."
translations.idiomatic: if Uyghurs came too, they should fall back to Heyang."

sentences.zh: 朝義不從。

translations.literal: Chaoyi did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi refused.

sentences.zh: 壬申，官軍至洛陽北郊，分兵取懷州；

translations.literal: On renshen, government armies reached Luoyang's northern suburbs and divided troops to take Huaizhou;
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day the allies reached Luoyang's north suburb and sent a column to take Huaizhou;

sentences.zh: 癸酉，拔之。

translations.literal: on guiyou, took it.
translations.idiomatic: capturing it on guiyou day.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，官軍陳於橫水。

translations.literal: On yihai, government armies arrayed at Hengshui.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the imperial army formed at Hengshui.

sentences.zh: 賊眾數萬，立柵自固，懷恩陳於西原以當之。

translations.literal: Rebel masses numbered tens of thousands, erected palisades to secure themselves—Huai'en arrayed on the western plain to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of rebels fortified a camp; Huai'en faced them on the west plain.

sentences.zh: 遣驍騎及回紇並南山出柵東北，表裡合擊，大破之。

translations.literal: He sent elite cavalry and Uyghurs along the southern mountain to exit northeast of the palisade—inner and outer combined attack, greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Elite cavalry and Uyghurs swept around the south hills and routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 朝義悉其精兵十萬救之，陳於昭覺寺，官軍驟擊之，殺傷甚眾，而賊陳不動；

translations.literal: Chaoyi gathered all his elite hundred thousand to rescue, arrayed at Zhaojue Temple—government armies suddenly attacked, killed and wounded very many, yet the rebel array did not move;
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi committed a hundred thousand elite troops at Zhaojue Temple; imperial assaults failed to break the line;

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩遣射生五百人力戰，賊雖多死者，陳亦如初。

translations.literal: Yu Chao'en sent five hundred archer-guards to fight hard—though rebels had many dead, the array was as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chao'en's five hundred archers killed many yet the rebel line held.

sentences.zh: 鎮西節度使馬璘曰：「事急矣！」

translations.literal: Zhenxi military governor Ma Lin said, "The affair is urgent!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhenxi governor Ma Lin cried that the moment was critical.

sentences.zh: 遂單騎奮擊，奪賊兩牌，突入萬眾中。

translations.literal: He then alone on horse charged fiercely, seized two rebel shields, and burst into ten thousand masses.
translations.idiomatic: He charged alone, snatched two enemy shields, and plunged into the enemy host.

sentences.zh: 賊左右披靡，大軍乘之而入，賊眾大敗；

translations.literal: Rebels left and right fell away; the great army rode the opening and entered—the rebel masses were greatly defeated;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke; the main force poured in and routed them;

sentences.zh: 轉戰於石榴園、老君廟，賊又敗；

translations.literal: fighting shifted to Shiliu Garden and Laojun Temple—rebels were again defeated;
translations.idiomatic: pursuit at Shiliu Garden and Laojun Temple brought further defeats;

sentences.zh: 人馬相蹂踐，填尚書谷，斬首六萬級，捕虜二萬人，朝義將輕騎數百東走。

translations.literal: men and horses trampled one another, filling Shangshu Valley—sixty thousand heads cut, twenty thousand captives—Chaoyi with several hundred light cavalry fled east.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty thousand heads were taken and Chaoyi fled east with a few hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 懷恩進克東京及河陽城，獲其中書令許叔冀、王胄等，制釋之。

translations.literal: Huai'en advanced and took the Eastern Capital and Heyang city, captured Zhongshu Director Xu Shuji, Wang Zhou, and others—edict released them.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en took Luoyang and Heyang and freed captives including Xu Shuji.

sentences.zh: 懷恩留回紇可汗營於河陽，使其子右廂兵馬使瑒及朔方兵馬使高輔成帥步騎萬餘乘勝逐朝義，至鄭州，再戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Huai'en left the Uyghur Qaghan encamped at Heyang, had his son Right Wing army horse commissioner Yang and Shuofang army horse commissioner Gao Fucheng lead more than ten thousand foot and horse in victory pursuit of Chaoyi—to Zhengzhou, twice fighting all successful.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en left the Uyghurs at Heyang and sent his son Yang and Gao Fucheng in pursuit to Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝義至汴州，其陳留節度使張獻誠閉門拒之；

translations.literal: Chaoyi reached Bianzhou—his Chenliu military governor Zhang Xiancheng closed gates and refused him;
translations.idiomatic: At Bianzhou Zhang Xiancheng shut Chaoyi out;

sentences.zh: 朝義奔濮州，獻誠開門出降。

translations.literal: "Chaoyi fled to Puzhou—Xiancheng opened gates and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: "Chaoyi fled to Puzhou while Xiancheng surrendered.

sentences.zh: 回紇入東京，肆行殺略，死者萬計，火累旬不滅。

translations.literal: Uyghurs entered the Eastern Capital, wantonly killed and plundered—dead numbered in the tens of thousands—fires burned for ten days without extinguishing.
translations.idiomatic: Uyghurs looted Luoyang, killing tens of thousands and burning the city for days.

sentences.zh: 朔方、神策軍亦以東京、鄭、汴、汝州皆為賊境，所過虜掠，三月乃已，比屋蕩盡，士民皆衣紙。

translations.literal: Shuofang and Shence armies also, because the Eastern Capital, Zheng, Bian, and Ruzhou were all rebel territory, wherever they passed they captured and plundered—for three months before it stopped; house after house was emptied, gentry and people all wore paper.
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang and Shence troops also looted for three months until towns were stripped bare and people wore paper clothing.

sentences.zh: 回紇悉置所掠寶貨於河陽，留其將安恪守之。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs all placed plundered treasure at Heyang and left their general An Shou to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs stored loot at Heyang under General An Shou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁丑，露布至京師。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on dingchou, victory bulletins reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dingchou day, victory reports reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 朝義自濮州北渡河，懷恩進攻滑州，拔之，追敗朝義於衛州。

translations.literal: Chaoyi from Puzhou crossed the river north—Huai'en advanced to attack Huazhou, took it, pursued and defeated Chaoyi at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi fled north from Puzhou; Huai'en took Huazhou and routed him at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 朝義睢陽節度使田承嗣等將兵四萬餘人與朝義合，復來拒戰；

translations.literal: Chaoyi's Suiyang military governor Tian Chengsi and others led more than forty thousand troops to join Chaoyi and again came to resist battle;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chengsi joined Chaoyi with forty thousand men to fight again;

sentences.zh: 僕固瑒擊破之，長驅至昌樂東。

translations.literal: Pugu Yang defeated them and drove long to east of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Yang broke them and pursued to east of Changle.

sentences.zh: 朝義帥魏州兵來戰，又敗走。

translations.literal: Chaoyi led Weizhou troops to fight and was again defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi led Weizhou troops but was beaten again.

sentences.zh: 於是鄴郡節度使薛嵩以相、衛、洺、邢四州降於陳鄭、澤潞節度使李抱玉，恆陽節度使張忠志以恆、趙、深、定、易五州降於河東節度使辛雲京。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ye Prefecture military governor Xue Song with Xiang, Wei, Ming, and Xing four prefectures surrendered to Chen-Zheng and Ze-Lu military governor Li Baoyu; Hengyang military governor Zhang Zhongzhi with Heng, Zhao, Shen, Ding, and Yi five prefectures surrendered to Hedong military governor Xin Yunjing.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Song surrendered four prefectures to Li Baoyu and Zhang Zhongzhi five to Xin Yunjing.

sentences.zh: 嵩，楚玉之子也。

translations.literal: Song was Chu Yu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Song was the son of Xue Chuyu.

sentences.zh: 抱玉等已進軍入其營，按其部伍，嵩等皆受代；

translations.literal: Baoyu and others had already advanced into their camps and inspected their ranks—Song and company all accepted replacement;
translations.idiomatic: Li Baoyu entered their camps to reorganize them;

sentences.zh: 居無何，僕固懷恩皆令復位。

translations.literal: before long Pugu Huai'en ordered all restored to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: but Huai'en soon restored them all.

sentences.zh: 由是抱玉、雲京疑懷恩有貳心，各表言之，朝廷密為之備；

translations.literal: Hence Baoyu and Yunjing suspected Huai'en had divided loyalty, each memorialized saying so—the court secretly prepared against it;
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu and Xin Yunjing suspected Huai'en's loyalty and warned the court;

sentences.zh: 懷恩亦上疏自理，上慰勉之。

translations.literal: Huai'en also submitted memorials explaining himself—the emperor comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en defended himself and the emperor reassured him.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，制：「東京及河南、北受偽官者，一切不問。」

translations.literal: On xinsi, an edict: "Those in the Eastern Capital and Henan and north who accepted false offices—all will not be questioned."
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day collaborators in Luoyang and the north were amnestied."

sentences.zh: 己丑，以戶部侍郎劉晏兼河南道水陸轉運都使。

translations.literal: On jichou, Hubu vice director Liu Yan was made concurrent Henan Circuit water and land transport overall commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day Liu Yan was named overall transport commissioner for Henan.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以張忠志為成德軍節度使，統恆、趙、深、定、易五州，賜姓李，名寶臣。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Zhang Zhongzhi was made Chengde army military governor, commanding Heng, Zhao, Shen, Ding, and Yi five prefectures—granted surname Li, name Bao Chen.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Zhang Zhongzhi became Chengde governor as Li Baochen.

sentences.zh: 初，辛雲京引兵將出井陘，常山裨將王武俊說寶臣曰：「今河東兵精銳，出境遠鬥，不可敵也。

translations.literal: Initially, Xin Yunjing was leading troops about to exit Jingxing Pass—Changshan staff general Wang Wujun said to Baochen, "Now Hedong troops are elite and sharp—fighting far outside borders, they cannot be matched.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun warned Li Baochen that Xin Yunjing's elite Hedong army could not be beaten in the field.

sentences.zh: 且吾以寡當眾，以曲遇直，戰則必離，守則必潰，公其圖之。」

translations.literal: Moreover we with few meet many, crooked meets straight—in battle we will surely scatter, in defense surely collapse—Your Excellency should plan for this."
translations.idiomatic: He urged surrender rather than fight a hopeless battle.

sentences.zh: 寶臣乃撤守備，舉五州來降。

translations.literal: Baochen then removed defenses and raised the five prefectures to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baochen surrendered the five prefectures.

sentences.zh: 及復為節度使，以武俊之策為善，擢為先鋒兵馬使。

translations.literal: When again made military governor, he considered Wujun's strategy good and promoted him to vanguard army horse commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Made governor again, he promoted Wang Wujun for the advice.

sentences.zh: 武俊，本契丹也，初名沿諾干。

translations.literal: "Wujun was originally Khitan—initial name Yannuogan.
translations.idiomatic: "Wang Wujun was Khitan, originally named Yannuogan.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀以僕固懷恩有平河朔功，請以副元帥讓之。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi, because Pugu Huai'en had merit in pacifying Hebei, requested to yield deputy supreme commander to him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi yielded deputy command to Huai'en for pacifying Hebei.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以懷恩為河北副元帥，加左僕射兼中書令、單于、鎮北大都護、朔方節度使。

translations.literal: On jihai, Huai'en was made Hebei deputy supreme commander, added Left Vice Director concurrent Zhongshu Director, Chanyu, Zhenbei Grand Protector, and Shuofang military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Huai'en became Hebei deputy commander with grand titles and Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 史朝義走至貝州，與其大將薛忠義等兩節度合，僕固瑒追之至臨清。

translations.literal: Shi Chaoyi fled to Beizhou, joined with his great generals Xue Zhongyi and two military governors—Pugu Yang pursued to Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi fled to Beizhou; Pugu Yang pursued to Linqing.

sentences.zh: 朝義自衡水引兵三萬還攻之，瑒設伏擊走之。

translations.literal: Chaoyi from Hengshui led thirty thousand troops back to attack—Yang set ambush and struck, driving him off.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi counterattacked from Hengshui with thirty thousand; Yang ambushed and repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 回紇又至，官軍益振，遂逐之；

translations.literal: Uyghurs again arrived—government armies grew more vigorous and thus pursued;
translations.idiomatic: Uyghur reinforcements bolstered the pursuit;

sentences.zh: 大戰於下博東南，賊大敗，積屍擁流而下，朝義奔莫州。

translations.literal: great battle southeast of Xiabo—rebels greatly defeated, piled corpses choked the current downstream—Chaoyi fled to Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiabo the rebels were shattered; Chaoyi fled to Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 懷恩都知兵馬使薛兼訓、兵馬使郝庭玉與田神功、辛雲京會於下博，進圍朝義於莫州，青淄節度使侯希逸繼至。

translations.literal: Huai'en Chief of Staff Xue Jianxun, army horse commissioner Hao Tingyu with Tian Shenggong and Xin Yunjing met at Xiabo, advanced to besiege Chaoyi at Mozhou—Qing-Zi military governor Hou Xiyi followed after.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en's generals besieged Chaoyi at Mozhou with Tian Shenggong, Xin Yunjing, and Hou Xiyi.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚申，初以太祖配天地。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on gengshen, first time Grand Ancestor was paired with Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Grand Ancestor was first paired with Heaven and Earth in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 代宗睿文孝武皇帝上之上

translations.literal: Above the first part of Emperor Daizong, Cultured in Text, Filially Martial
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong, first section

sentences.zh: 肅宗文明武德大聖大宣孝皇帝下之下廣德元年（

translations.literal: Below the second part of Emperor Suzong—the first year of Guangde (
translations.idiomatic: First year of Guangde, continuing from Emperor Suzong (

sentences.zh: 癸卯，公元七六三年）

translations.literal: guimao, CE 763)
translations.idiomatic: 763 CE, year guimao)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己卯，追謚吳太后曰章敬皇后。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the day jimao, posthumous title for Empress Dowager Wu as Empress Zhangjing.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on jimao day, Empress Dowager Wu was posthumously titled Zhangjing.

sentences.zh: 癸未，以國子祭酒劉晏為吏部尚書、同平章事，度支等使如故。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Guozi Chancellor Liu Yan was made Libu Minister and fellow Grand Councillor, revenue commissioners as before.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day Liu Yan became minister of personnel and grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 初，來瑱在襄陽，程元振有所請托，不從；

translations.literal: Initially, Lai Tian at Xiangyang—Cheng Yuanzhen had requests entrusted, not followed;
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang Lai Tian had refused Cheng Yuanzhen's favors;

sentences.zh: 及為相，元振譖瑱言涉不順。

translations.literal: when made chancellor, Yuanzhen slandered Tian saying words touched on disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: as chancellor Yuanzhen accused him of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 王仲升在賊中，以屈服得全，賊平得歸，與元振善，奏瑱與賊合謀，致仲升陷賊。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongsheng among rebels, by submitting was preserved—when rebels pacified returned, friendly with Yuanzhen—memorialized Tian colluded with rebels causing Zhongsheng trapped among rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongsheng, who had surrendered to rebels, joined Yuanzhen in accusing Lai Tian of collusion.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，瑱坐削官爵，流播州，賜死於路。

translations.literal: On renyin, Tian was punished by stripping rank and title, exiled to Bozhou—granted death on the road.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day Lai Tian was stripped of rank, exiled, and executed en route.

sentences.zh: 由是籓鎮皆切齒於元振。

translations.literal: Henceforth frontier garrisons all gnashed teeth at Yuanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier governors thereafter hated Yuanzhen.

sentences.zh: 史朝義屢出戰，皆敗，田承嗣說朝義，令親往幽州發兵，還救莫州，承嗣自請留守莫州。

translations.literal: Shi Chaoyi repeatedly sallied and all were defeated—Tian Chengsi persuaded Chaoyi to go personally to Youzhou to raise troops and return to rescue Mozhou—Chengsi himself requested to remain guarding Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated defeats Tian Chengsi urged Chaoyi to fetch troops from Youzhou while he held Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 朝義從之，選精騎五千自北門犯圍而出。

translations.literal: Chaoyi followed, selected five thousand elite cavalry and broke the siege exiting the north gate.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi broke out north with five thousand elite horsemen.

sentences.zh: 朝義既去，承嗣即以城降，送朝義母、妻、子於官軍。

translations.literal: Once Chaoyi had gone, Chengsi immediately surrendered the city and sent Chaoyi's mother, wife, and children to the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi then surrendered Mozhou and sent Chaoyi's family to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 於是僕固瑒、侯希逸、薛兼訓等帥眾三萬追之，及于歸義，與戰，朝義敗走。

translations.literal: Thereupon Pugu Yang, Hou Xiyi, Xue Jianxun and others led thirty thousand in pursuit, caught up at Guiyi, fought—Chaoyi defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Yang and allies pursued with thirty thousand and defeated Chaoyi at Guiyi.

sentences.zh: 時朝義范陽節度使李懷仙已因中使駱奉仙請降，遣兵馬使李抱忠將兵三千鎮范陽縣，朝義至范陽，不得入。

translations.literal: At that time Chaoyi's Fanyang military governor Li Huaixian had already through palace envoy Luo Fengxian requested surrender, sent army horse commissioner Li Baozhong to lead three thousand troops to garrison Fanyang county—Chaoyi reached Fanyang and could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaixian had already surrendered Fanyang; Li Baozhong blocked Chaoyi's entry.

sentences.zh: 官軍將至，朝義遣人諭抱忠以大軍留莫州、輕騎來發兵救援之意，因責以君臣之義，抱忠對曰：「天不祚燕，唐室復興。

translations.literal: Government armies were about to arrive—Chaoyi sent men to instruct Baozhong that the great army remained at Mozhou and light cavalry came to raise troops for rescue, thereby reproaching him with lord-and-minister righteousness—Baozhong answered, "Heaven does not bless Yan—the Tang house revives.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi appealed to duty; Baozhong replied heaven favored the Tang, not Yan.

sentences.zh: 今既歸唐矣，豈可更為反覆，獨不愧三軍邪！

translations.literal: Now having already returned to Tang, how can one again be flip-flop—alone not ashamed before the three armies!
translations.idiomatic: Having submitted to Tang, how could he turn traitor again before his troops?

sentences.zh: 大丈夫恥以詭計相圖，願早擇去就以謀自全。

translations.literal: A great man is ashamed to plot with crafty schemes—wish early to choose departure or stay to plan self-preservation.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Chaoyi to choose his fate honestly.

sentences.zh: 且田承嗣必已叛矣，不然，官軍何以得至此！」

translations.literal: Moreover Tian Chengsi must already have rebelled—otherwise how could government armies reach here!"
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chengsi must have betrayed you—else how did the Tang army reach here?"

sentences.zh: 朝義大懼，曰：「吾朝來未食，獨不能以一餐相餉乎！」

translations.literal: Chaoyi was greatly afraid and said, "Since morning I have not eaten—can you not alone offer one meal!"
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Chaoyi begged for a meal.

sentences.zh: 抱忠乃令人設食於城東。

translations.literal: Baozhong then had people set food east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhong fed him east of the city.

sentences.zh: 於是范陽人在朝義麾下者，並拜辭而去，朝義涕泣而已，獨與胡騎數百既食而去。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fanyang men under Chaoyi's command all bowed farewell and left—Chaoyi wept tears only, alone with several hundred Hu cavalry after eating departed.
translations.idiomatic: His Fanyang followers deserted; Chaoyi left with only a few hundred Hu horsemen.

sentences.zh: 東奔廣陽，廣陽不受；

translations.literal: Fled east to Guangyang—Guangyang did not accept;
translations.idiomatic: Guangyang refused him;

sentences.zh: 欲北入奚、契丹，至溫泉柵，李懷仙兵追及之；

translations.literal: wished north into Xi and Khitan—reached Wenquan palisade, Li Huaixian's troops caught up;
translations.idiomatic: fleeing toward the Xi and Khitan he was caught at Wenquan;

sentences.zh: 朝義窮蹙，縊於林中，懷仙取其首以獻。

translations.literal: Chaoyi cornered, hanged himself in the woods—Huaixian took his head and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi hanged himself; Huaixian sent his head to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩與諸軍皆還。

translations.literal: "Pugu Huai'en and all armies returned.
translations.idiomatic: "Huai'en and the allied armies withdrew.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，朝義首至京師。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Chaoyi's head reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day Chaoyi's head reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 閏月，己酉夜，有回紇十五人犯含光門，突入鴻臚寺，門司不敢遏。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, on the night of jiyou, fifteen Uyghurs violated Hanguang Gate and burst into Honglu Temple—the gate office did not dare stop them.
translations.idiomatic: On an intercalary jiyou night fifteen Uyghurs forced Hanguang Gate into Honglu Temple unchecked.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以史朝義降將薛嵩為相、衛、邢、洺、貝、磁六州節度使，田承嗣為魏、博、德、滄、瀛五州都防禦使，李懷仙仍故地為幽州、盧龍節度使。

translations.literal: On guihai, Shi Chaoyi's surrendering general Xue Song was made six-prefecture military governor of Xiang, Wei, Xing, Ming, Bei, and Ci; Tian Chengsi five-prefecture overall defense commissioner of Wei, Bo, De, Cang, and Ying; Li Huaixian on former territory as Youzhou and Lulong military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day former rebels Xue Song, Tian Chengsi, and Li Huaixian were enfeoffed over Hebei.

sentences.zh: 時河北諸州皆已降，嵩等迎僕固懷恩，拜於馬首，乞行間自效；

translations.literal: At that time all Hebei prefectures had surrendered—Song and company welcomed Pugu Huai'en, bowed at his horse's head, begged to serve in the interval;
translations.idiomatic: They bowed to Huai'en and offered service;

sentences.zh: 懷恩亦恐賊平寵衰，故奏留嵩等及李寶臣分帥河北，自為黨援。

translations.literal: Huai'en also feared when rebels were pacified favor would fade—therefore memorialized to retain Song and company and Li Baochen to divide command of Hebei, making his own factional support.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en kept them as Hebei governors to preserve his power.

sentences.zh: 朝廷亦厭苦兵革，敬冀無事，因而授之。

translations.literal: The court also wearied of war, respectfully hoped for no trouble, and thus granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The weary court accepted to keep peace.

sentences.zh: 回紇登裡可汗歸國，其部眾所過抄掠，廩給小不如意，輒殺人，無所忌憚。

translations.literal: Uyghur Tengri Qaghan returned home—his followers wherever they passed plundered; if granary provisions slightly displeased, they killed people without any dread.
translations.idiomatic: Returning home, Tengri's Uyghurs looted and killed over minor supply disputes.

sentences.zh: 陳鄭、澤潞節度使李抱玉欲遣官屬置頓，人人辭憚，趙城尉馬燧獨請行。

translations.literal: Chen-Zheng and Ze-Lu military governor Li Baoyu wished to dispatch officials to arrange halts—everyone declined in fear—Zhaocheng district magistrate Ma Sui alone requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baoyu needed an official to manage Uyghur passage; only Ma Sui volunteered.

sentences.zh: 比回紇將至，燧先遣人賂其渠帥，約毋暴掠，帥遣之旗曰：「有犯令者，君處戮之。」

translations.literal: When Uyghurs were about to arrive, Sui first sent men to bribe their chieftains, agreeing no violent plunder—the chieftain sent him a banner saying, "Whoever violates orders—you execute them."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui bribed Uyghur chiefs and received authority to punish violators.

sentences.zh: 燧取死囚為左右，小有違令，立斬之。

translations.literal: Sui took condemned prisoners as attendants—slight violation of orders, immediately beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He executed prisoners on the spot for minor infractions to terrify the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 回紇相顧失色，涉其境者皆拱手遵約束。

translations.literal: Uyghurs looked at one another and lost color—those crossing his territory all clasped hands obeying restrictions.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs behaved; all who passed obeyed.

sentences.zh: 抱玉奇之，燧因說抱玉曰：「燧與回紇言，頗得其情。

translations.literal: Baoyu marveled—Sui therefore said to Baoyu, "Sui in speaking with Uyghurs rather grasped their sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui warned Baoyu that he understood the Uyghurs and Huai'en's ambitions.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩恃功驕蹇，其子瑒好勇而輕，今內樹四帥，外交回紇，必有窺河東、澤潞之志，宜深備之。」

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en relies on merit, proud and obstinate—his son Yang loves bravery and is rash—now within he plants four commanders, outwardly allies Uyghurs—surely has mind to eye Hedong and Ze-Lu—should deeply guard against it."
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en, arrogant with four Hebei clients and Uyghur allies, likely coveted Hedong and Ze-Lu.

sentences.zh: 抱玉然之。

translations.literal: Baoyu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baoyu agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，長安人梁崇義以羽林射生從來瑱鎮襄陽，累遷右兵馬使。

translations.literal: Initially, Chang'an man Liang Chongyi as Yulin archer-guard followed Lai Tian to guard Xiangyang, repeatedly promoted to Right army horse commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chongyi had followed Lai Tian to Xiangyang as a guardsman.

sentences.zh: 崇義有勇力，能卷鐵舒鉤，沉毅寡言，得眾心。

translations.literal: Chongyi had courage and strength, could curl iron and bend hooks, was deep, steady, and sparing of words—won people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Strong and taciturn, he won the troops' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 瑱之入朝也，命諸將分戍諸州；

translations.literal: When Tian entered court he ordered generals to divide garrison among prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Lai Tian had dispersed his generals to garrison posts;

sentences.zh: 瑱死，戍者皆奔歸襄陽。

translations.literal: Tian died—the garrison men all ran back to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: when he died they rushed back to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 行軍司馬龐充將兵二千赴河南，至汝州，聞瑱死，引兵還襲襄州；

translations.literal: Campaign marshal Pang Chong led two thousand troops toward Henan—reaching Ruzhou, hearing Tian died, led troops back to raid Xiangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Pang Chong turned back from Ruzhou to seize Xiangzhou;

sentences.zh: 左兵馬使李昭拒之，充奔房州。

translations.literal: Left army horse commissioner Li Zhao resisted—Chong fled to Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhao repulsed him and Pang fled to Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇義自鄧州引戍兵歸，與昭及副使薛南陽相讓為長，久之不決，眾皆曰：「兵非梁卿主之不可。」

translations.literal: Chongyi from Dengzhou led garrison troops back, with Zhao and deputy Xue Nanyang mutually yielding seniority—long undecided—all said, "The army without Director Liang's command cannot stand."
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chongyi returned from Dengzhou; after a leadership dispute the troops chose him.

sentences.zh: 遂推崇義為帥。

translations.literal: They then elevated Chongyi as commander.
translations.idiomatic: They made Liang Chongyi commander.

sentences.zh: 崇義尋昭及南陽，以其狀聞，上不能討。

translations.literal: Chongyi tracked Zhao and Nanyang, reported the situation—the emperor could not punish.
translations.idiomatic: He eliminated rivals and reported to court, which could not punish him.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲辰，以崇義為襄州刺史、山南東道節度留後。

translations.literal: Third month, on jiachen, Chongyi was made Xiangzhou prefect and Shannan East military governor acting regent.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day in the third month he was confirmed as Shannan East regent.

sentences.zh: 崇義奏改葬瑱，為之立祠，不居瑱聽事及正堂。

translations.literal: "Chongyi memorialized to reburial Tian, built a shrine for him, did not occupy Tian's reception hall or main hall.
translations.idiomatic: "He reburied Lai Tian with honors but did not occupy his hall.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，葬至道大聖大明孝皇帝於泰陵；

translations.literal: On xinyou, buried Emperor Zhidao Dasheng Daming Xiaozong at Tailing;
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the retired Emperor Xuanzong was buried at Tailing;

sentences.zh: 廟號玄宗。

translations.literal: temple name Xuanzong.
translations.idiomatic: temple name Xuanzong.

sentences.zh: 庚午，葬文明武德大聖大宣孝皇帝於喬陵；

translations.literal: On gengwu, buried Emperor Wenming Wude Dasheng Daxuan Xiaozong at Qiaoling;
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Emperor Suzong was buried at Qiaoling;

sentences.zh: 廟號肅宗。

translations.literal: temple name Suzong.
translations.idiomatic: temple name Suzong.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚辰，李光弼奏擒袁晃，浙東皆平。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on gengchen, Li Guangbi memorialized capturing Yuan Huang—Zhedong all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Guangbi reported capturing Yuan Huang and pacifying Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 時晁聚眾近二十萬，轉攻州縣，光弼使部將張伯儀將兵討平之。

translations.literal: At that time Chao gathered masses near two hundred thousand, turned to attack prefectures and counties—Guangbi had subordinate general Zhang Boyi lead troops to suppress and pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chao had mustered two hundred thousand; Zhang Boyi crushed him.

sentences.zh: 伯儀，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Boyi was a man of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Boyi came from Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀數上言：「吐蕃、党項不可忽，宜早為之備。」

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi repeatedly submitted: "Tibet and Tangut must not be slighted—should early prepare against them."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi repeatedly warned against neglecting Tibet and the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，遣兼御史大夫李之芳等使於吐蕃，為虜所留，二年乃得歸。

translations.literal: "On xinchou, sent Concurrent Censor Grandee Li Zhifang and others as envoys to Tibet—detained by the enemy, only after two years could return."
translations.idiomatic: "On xinchou envoys to Tibet were detained for two years."

sentences.zh: 群臣三上表請立太子；

translations.literal: Ministers thrice submitted memorials requesting installation of Crown Prince;
translations.idiomatic: Ministers thrice asked to name a crown prince;

sentences.zh: 五月，癸卯，詔許俟秋成議之。

translations.literal: fifth month, on guimao, edict permitted waiting until autumn harvest to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: on guimao day in the fifth month the emperor deferred until after harvest.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，制分河北諸州：以幽、莫、媯、檀、平、薊為幽州管；

translations.literal: On dingmao, edict divided Hebei prefectures: You, Mo, Gui, Tan, Ping, and Ji as Youzhou circuit;
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day Hebei was divided into circuits:

sentences.zh: 恆、定、趙、深、易為成德軍管；

translations.literal: Heng, Ding, Zhao, Shen, and Yi as Chengde army circuit;
translations.idiomatic: Chengde over five prefectures;

sentences.zh: 相、貝、邢、洺為相州管；

translations.literal: Xiang, Bei, Xing, and Ming as Xiangzhou circuit;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang circuit over four prefectures;

sentences.zh: 魏、博、德為魏州管；

translations.literal: Wei, Bo, and De as Weizhou circuit;
translations.idiomatic: Wei circuit over three;

sentences.zh: 滄、棣、冀、瀛為青淄管；

translations.literal: Cang, Di, Ji, and Ying as Qing-Zi circuit;
translations.idiomatic: Qing-Zi over four;

sentences.zh: 懷、衛、河陽為澤潞管。

translations.literal: Huai, Wei, and Heyang as Ze-Lu circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Ze-Lu over Huai, Wei, and Heyang.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸酉，禮部侍郎華陰楊綰上疏，以為：「古之選士必取行實，近世專尚文辭。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on guiyou, Libu vice director Huayin Yang Guan submitted memorial, holding: "Ancient selection of scholars must take conduct and reality—in recent ages they exclusively honor literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yang Guan argued that officials should be chosen for conduct, not literary flair alone.

sentences.zh: 自隋煬帝始置進士科，猶試策而已；

translations.literal: From Sui Emperor Yang establishing the jinshi category, it was still only testing policy essays;
translations.idiomatic: Since Sui Yangdi's jinshi degree tested policy essays;

sentences.zh: 至高宗時，考功員外郎劉思立始奏進士加雜文，明經加帖，從此積弊，轉而成俗。

translations.literal: reaching Gaozong's time, Examination Bureau section director Liu Sili first memorialized adding miscellaneous essays for jinshi and paste essays for mingjing—from this accumulated abuses, turning into custom.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sili added literary essays, beginning abuses that became custom.

sentences.zh: 朝之公卿以此待士，家之長老以此訓子，其明經則誦貼括以求僥倖。

translations.literal: Court grandees treat scholars thus, family elders train sons thus—for mingjing they recite paste summaries seeking luck.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and families alike drilled paste summaries for mingjing exams to game the system.

sentences.zh: 又，舉人皆令投牒自應，如此，欲其返淳樸，崇廉讓，何可得也！

translations.literal: Moreover, examination candidates are all ordered to submit memorials and self-recommend—like this, wishing them return to simplicity, honor integrity and yielding—how can it be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: Self-nomination exams could not restore simplicity or humility, he argued.

sentences.zh: 請令縣令察孝廉，取行著鄉閭、學知經術薦之於州。

translations.literal: Request ordering county magistrates to inspect filial and incorrupt, take those whose conduct shines in villages and hamlets and who study knowing classics, recommend to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed county magistrates recommend men of local virtue and classical learning.

sentences.zh: 剌史考試，升之於省。

translations.literal: Prefects examine and promote them to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects would examine them and send the best to the capital.

sentences.zh: 任各佔一經，朝廷擇儒學之士，問經義二十條，對策三道，上第即注官，中第得出身，下第罷歸。

translations.literal: Each assigned one classic—the court selects Confucian scholars, asks twenty items on classic meaning, three policy responses—top grade then office appointment, middle grade obtains entry rank, lower grade dismissed home.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates would be tested on one classic; top passes received office, middling entry rank, failures went home.

sentences.zh: 又，道舉亦非理國所資，望與明經、進士並停。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Daoist recommendations also are not resources for ordering the state—hope together with mingjing and jinshi all suspended."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged abolishing Daoist recruitment along with mingjing and jinshi.

sentences.zh: 上命諸司通議，給事中李棲筠、左丞賈至、京兆尹嚴武並與綰同。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered all offices to discuss jointly—Palace Attendant Li Qiyun, Left Vice Director Jia Zhi, and Jingzhao prefect Yan Wu all agreed with Guan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered debate; Li Qiyun, Jia Zhi, and Yan Wu sided with Yang Guan.

sentences.zh: 至議以為：「今試學者以帖字為精通，考文者以聲病為是非，風流頹弊，誠當厘改。

translations.literal: Zhi's deliberation held: "Now testing scholars by paste characters as mastery, examining writing by tonal defects as right and wrong—style decadent and corrupt, truly should be rectified.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Zhi agreed the exam culture was corrupt and needed reform.

sentences.zh: 然自東晉以來，人多僑寓，士居鄉土，百無一二；

translations.literal: Yet from Eastern Jin onward many people sojourn abroad—scholars dwelling in native soil, not one or two in a hundred;
translations.idiomatic: But since Eastern Jin few scholars still lived in their home districts;

sentences.zh: 請兼廣學校，保桑梓者鄉里舉焉，在流寓者癢序推焉。」

translations.literal: request also broadly expand schools—those keeping ancestral lands recommended by village and hamlet, those dwelling in exile promoted by academies."
translations.idiomatic: he proposed expanding schools to recommend natives locally and sojourners through academies.

sentences.zh: 敕禮部具條目以聞。

translations.literal: Edict ordered Libu to prepare articles and report.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites was ordered to draft rules.

sentences.zh: 綰又請置五經秀才科。

translations.literal: "Guan also requested establishing Five Classics xiucai category.
translations.idiomatic: "Yang Guan also proposed a Five Classics xiucai examination.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以魏博都防禦使田承嗣為節度使。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Wei-Bo overall defense commissioner Tian Chengsi was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day Tian Chengsi became full military governor of Wei-Bo.

sentences.zh: 承嗣舉管內戶口，壯者皆籍為兵，惟使老弱耕稼，數年間有眾十萬；

translations.literal: Chengsi raised registered population within his circuit—all able-bodied registered as soldiers, only allowing old and weak to farm—within several years had masses of one hundred thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi registered every able man as a soldier, leaving only the old and weak to farm, building an army of one hundred thousand;

sentences.zh: 又選其驍健者萬人自衛，謂之牙兵。

translations.literal: again selected ten thousand of their fierce and strong for self-guard—called yamen troops.
translations.idiomatic: and chose ten thousand elite guards called yamen troops.

sentences.zh: 同華節度使李懷讓為程元振所譖，恐懼，自殺。

translations.literal: Tong-Hua military governor Li Huairang was slandered by Cheng Yuanzhen, feared, and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Tong-Hua governor Li Huairang, slandered by Cheng Yuanzhen, committed suicide.
